title: Criminal past of Illinois ethanol plant bomb scare suspect includes multiple felonies, 2 prison stints
summary: Andrew Kozak, the BioUrja worker accused in the Peoria bomb threat, has a criminal past spanning four Nebraska counties, Fox News Digital reports.
story: FBI Special Agent in Charge Ryan Presley commends law enforcement partners after a credible explosive device is found in Peoria. Presley urges the public to report suspicious behavior to help defend the homeland.

An Illinois ethanol plant worker with a lengthy criminal past was federally indicted Tuesday after prosecutors said he emailed a threat claiming explosive devices had been placed at the facility where he worked.
A federal grand jury indicted Andrew M. Kozak on Tuesday on charges of threats regarding explosives and interstate communications of a threat.
Prosecutors allege Kozak emailed BioUrja Renewables on Friday indicating that explosive devices had been placed at the company's Peoria facility.
LIVE EXPLOSIVE DEVICE FOUND NEAR HOMELAND SECURITY OFFICE IN CLEVELAND, FORCING MASS EVACUATIONS
The email threatened to damage and destroy a building and other property "by means of fire and an explosive," according to the indictment.
Federal investigators swarmed a sprawling Illinois ethanol plant that spans 44½ football fields. (FBI Springfield Office)

NBC Chicago previously reported that Kozak, 41, of Chillicothe, had worked at BioUrja for about 10 months and allegedly planted the explosive device before sending the threat, citing federal law enforcement sources.
The indictment does not accuse Kozak of physically planting the explosive device found at the facility.

During a news conference Tuesday, federal officials declined to say who built or planted the explosive device, how many devices were involved or how powerful the device was. They also would not say whether anyone else may have been involved.
FBI Springfield Special Agent in Charge Ryan Presley said most bomb threats investigated by law enforcement are ultimately deemed not credible.
"But in this instance, it was," Presley said. "Had it not been for the swift action of the responders and the bomb technicians, this incident could have had a very different outcome."
Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon said about 2,500 homes were evacuated as authorities responded to the threat.

Kozak returned to BioUrja for work Monday morning and was taken into custody when he arrived, NBC Chicago reported, citing federal sources. FBI agents also executed a search warrant at his Chillicothe home, according to the outlet.
Kozak has a criminal past that includes several burglary-related felony convictions across four Nebraska counties and two stints in state prison, records reviewed by Fox News Digital show.
Andrew Kozak, 41, was federally indicted Tuesday on charges stemming from an emailed threat involving explosive devices at the BioUrja Renewables plant in Peoria, Illinois. (Andrew Kozak/LinkedIn)
Kozak's criminal history stretches back two decades.
Court and corrections records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Kozak was convicted of multiple burglary-related felonies across Platte, Polk, Nance and Colfax counties in Nebraska.
In Platte County, Kozak pleaded no contest to three felony burglary charges after initially facing seven burglary counts and one attempted burglary charge.
A judge found him guilty and determined Kozak was "not a fit and proper person" for probation before sentencing him to three to five years in prison.
Kozak was also convicted in two Polk County felony burglary cases. One court record identifies Osceola High School, while another shows Kozak was ordered to pay restitution to Osceola Public Schools.
In Nance County, Kozak was convicted of attempted felony burglary and sentenced to 20 months to five years in prison.
MASSIVE CHEMICAL FIRE ERUPTS AT ELECTRICAL TRANSFORMER PLANT IN MISSISSIPPI, FORCING EVACUATION

The BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, where authorities discovered an explosive device Friday, prompting a one-mile evacuation and a federal investigation. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)
Nebraska corrections records show Kozak was released on discretionary parole in August 2008.

He later returned to state prison on a separate Colfax County burglary conviction carrying a three-to-five-year sentence. Kozak was released on discretionary parole in October 2014, and his parole expired in May 2015.
CAR LOADED WITH EXPLOSIVES SLAMS INTO LAVISH PORTLAND SOCIAL CLUB, BOMB SQUAD STILL PULLING OUT LIVE DEVICES
The investigation began Friday afternoon when workers at BioUrja reported receiving a bomb threat. About an hour later, authorities located a suspicious package near the facility.
The device was deemed a credible threat, triggering the evacuation of homes and businesses within a one-mile radius.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
"I can just tell you it was deemed a credible threat," Dixon said Saturday. "There's an extensive criminal investigation going on."
Authorities warned that BioUrja houses large quantities of ethanol and other highly combustible materials, raising concerns about the potential consequences of an ignition.
Bomb technicians rendered the device safe, and authorities searched the facility without finding additional suspicious devices. The evacuation order was lifted Saturday after nearly a full day.

No injuries were reported.

title: South Carolina mother reveals troubling past of ex accused of burying their baby alive
summary: Koah Sharp's mother speaks out after the 11-month-old was found buried alive in a dog crate during a massive law enforcement search in South Carolina.
story: Dezarae Sharp, the mother of an 11-month-old boy allegedly buried alive by his father in South Carolina, spoke about her ex-boyfriend's troubling behavior and history of violence.
A South Carolina mother is speaking out after her baby was found buried alive inside a dog crate on Nov. 10, leading to an attempted murder charge against her ex-boyfriend.

Koah Sharp, just 11 months old, was allegedly buried alive in a crate for approximately 24 hours by his father, Michael Comer. title: MICHAEL RUIZ: New York's gutted police unit was more than a protest squad
summary: Zohran Mamdani is dissolving the NYPD Strategic Response Group for a civilian-led de-escalation plan critics say will embolden criminals and terrorists.
story: Terrorists and other criminals choose the path of least resistance, says retired FBI agent James Gagliano, making NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani's decision to disband a fast-acting deterrent group risky.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is dissolving the NYPD's Strategic Response Group — an elite tactical unit criticized for its handling of some left-wing protests while also responding to critical threats including a mass shooting at an office building last year and an attempted bombing attack on dueling demonstrations outside the city's mayoral residence.

"I think it’s one more step towards emboldening the criminals, emboldening the anarchists and emboldening the terrorists," said James Gagliano, a retired FBI supervisory special agent and Fox News contributor who spent years working alongside the NYPD.

Mamdani announced that the group will be dissolved at a news briefing early Monday. He had campaigned on the issue in part due to the unit's role in responding to organized protests — and riots — including those that exploded after George Floyd's death in 2020, demonstrations against Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Israel's war with Palestinian Hamas terrorists.
MAMDANI GUTS ELITE NYPD TACTICAL UNIT, BACKS 'CIVILIAN-LED APPROACH' TO RESPONDING TO PROTESTS

A looter takes an armful of clothing out of a store with a broken window in Manhattan, New York on June 1, 2020, following protests in the aftermath of the death of George Floyd in Minnesota. (J. Conrad Williams Jr./Newsday via Getty Images)

"New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat," Mamdani told reporters in a news briefing announcing the changes. "We are establishing a new, civilian-led approach that prioritizes dialogue, engagement and de-escalation."

Kettling — The SRG was involved in breaking up a protest using the so-called kettling technique, which involves surrounding and corralling marchers to control their movements. A June 4, 2020, incident cost city taxpayers millions after arrestees filed a lawsuit. Some related protests involved rioting, looting and vandalism and caused an estimated $1 billion to $2 billion across the country.Anti-Israel protests at Columbia University — The SRG was involved in the NYPD's response after agitators occupied the school's Hamilton Hall building.NFL Headquarters mass shooting — The SRG helped sweep floor-by-floor after a gunman opened fire in a Park Avenue office building, killing four.ICE protests — SRG officers have arrested demonstrators at anti-immigration enforcement protests this year.Gracie Mansion bombing — The SRG responded after two alleged ISIS supporters attempted to blow up a protest outside the city's mayoral residence, according to federal prosecutors. Their bombs failed to detonate, and NYPD Chief Aaron Edwards and Sgt. Luis Navarro tackled them at the scene.

Kettling — The SRG was involved in breaking up a protest using the so-called kettling technique, which involves surrounding and corralling marchers to control their movements. A June 4, 2020, incident cost city taxpayers millions after arrestees filed a lawsuit. Some related protests involved rioting, looting and vandalism and caused an estimated $1 billion to $2 billion across the country.
Anti-Israel protests at Columbia University — The SRG was involved in the NYPD's response after agitators occupied the school's Hamilton Hall building.
NFL Headquarters mass shooting — The SRG helped sweep floor-by-floor after a gunman opened fire in a Park Avenue office building, killing four.
ICE protests — SRG officers have arrested demonstrators at anti-immigration enforcement protests this year.

Gracie Mansion bombing — The SRG responded after two alleged ISIS supporters attempted to blow up a protest outside the city's mayoral residence, according to federal prosecutors. Their bombs failed to detonate, and NYPD Chief Aaron Edwards and Sgt. Luis Navarro tackled them at the scene.

Emir Balat flees after throwing a homemade explosive device towards police as NYPD Chief Aaron Edwards and Sgt. Luis Navarro take action during a protest in front of Gracie Mansion, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani's official residence, in New York on March 7, 2026. (CHARLY TRIBALLEAU/AFP via Getty Images)

The mayor plans to replace the SRG with several new programs by next spring. First is an unarmed Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD). This civilian team won't have arrest authority. It will work with a new First Amendment Support Team (FAST), consisting of 30 uniformed officers with specialized training in communication and de-escalation, according to Mamdani's office.

Lastly, his overhaul includes the creation of a new Patrol Support Division consisting of officers who will be trained in crowd control but spend most of their time on patrol duties. Counterterrorism duties will be consolidated in the NYPD's Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau.
MAMDANI PREPARES TO FULFILL PROMISE TO AXE NYPD UNIT RESPONSIBLE FOR CONTROLLING PROTEST VIOLENCE
Emir Balat was tackled by a law enforcement officer after he allegedly threw a bomb. (FNTV)

But the SRG has a varied role. While members are on hand for crowd control at large demonstrations, they also protect the protesters from outside threats. And they are positioned at other events involving large crowds, including the city's many parades, the iconic New Year's ball drop and other large events that take place every year.
"What the Strategic Response Group was designed to do was to be a highly mobile, well-trained, well-equipped group, like a senior SWAT team," Gagliano told Fox News Digital.
Unlike the NYPD's SWAT team, known as its Emergency Services Unit, the SRG also has a public-facing role, Gagliano said.
"Part of that was being on the front lines, the deterrent effect, and I think that's something that we're losing as well," he said.
ALLEGED ISIS-INSPIRED TERROR SUSPECTS LEFT FEDS ‘VOLUMINOUS’ DIGITAL TRAIL, FAMILY BREAKS DOWN IN TEARS

This image from surveillance video obtained by The Associated Press shows Shane Tamura outside a Manhattan office building on Monday, July 28, 2025. Tamura killed himself and four others in an office building housing the NFL headquarters, and the city's medical examiner later said his brain showed "unambiguous" signs of chronic traumatic encephalopathy, also known as CTE. (AP)
Terrorists and other criminals targeting public events tend to pick soft targets and the path of least resistance, he added.
"The Strategic Response Group was a deterrent, and it probably caused some people to decide, ‘Yeah, I’m not gonna try that. I’m not gonna do that,'" he said.
POLICE GROUPS CONDEMN MAMDANI OVER AXING ELITE NYPD UNIT
The unit has also been deployed around large public events with the goal of responding rapidly when needed, Gagliano said.

"The uniform folks are there for a deterrent effect," he said. "The uniform folks kept in abeyance like SRG, that are rolled out quickly and mobilized and strategically placed so that they can get to different spots very quickly."
Students and others demonstrate during a protest outside the gates to the Columbia University main campus in New York City on April 21. (Reuters/Ryan Murphy)
MAMDANI’S FIRST 100-PLUS DAYS: FAR-LEFT MAYOR FLUNKS A KEY LEADERSHIP TEST
Vincent J. Vallelong, president of the NYPD Sergeants Benevolent Association, brought up the failed Gracie Mansion bombing Monday.

"When an alleged terrorist attack threatened lives near Gracie Mansion, NYPD Sgt. Luis Navarro and Chief Aaron Edwards ran toward danger," Vallelong said in a statement. "Their decisive actions should be a lesson for Mayor Mamdani."
HAMAS, HEZBOLLAH FLAGS FLY AT ANTI-ISRAEL PROTEST MINUTES AFTER MAMDANI CONDEMNS TERROR PLOT AGAINST JEWS

Two allegedly ISIS-inspired men, Emir Balat and Ibrahim Kayumi, were arrested after federal prosecutors say they threw improvised explosive devices at a crowd outside the mayor's home and at a group of police as left- and right-wing protesters demonstrated across from one another. The bombs failed to explode.
Protesters are arrested on Park Avenue in New York City, June 5, 2020, as they defy the 8 p.m. curfew while protesting the death of George Floyd. (TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images)
According to federal prosecutors, Balat allegedly told police he had wanted the attack to be "bigger" than the Boston Marathon Bombing, which killed three and injured hundreds in 2013.
MAMDANI UNVEILS SWEEPING NYPD USE-OF-FORCE REVIEW, BUT STOPS SHORT OF FULFILLING KEY CAMPAIGN PROMISES
The SRG also deployed to help search for the gunman floor-by-floor after the mass shooting inside a Manhattan office building that houses the NFL’s headquarters on Park Avenue.
SEND US A TIP

Shattered glass lies in front of a looted souvenir and electronics shop near Times Square after a night of protests and vandalism over the death of George Floyd early June 2, 2020, in New York City. (John Moore/Getty Images)
Vallelong scoffed at the idea that the unarmed CDDD will protect the public from similar violent plots.

"Unarmed civilians cannot talk a determined attacker out of detonating a bomb," he said. "I fear this approach will embolden violent agitators to infiltrate peaceful demonstrations, putting protesters, police and bystanders at risk."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
People loot a store during demonstrations over the death of George Floyd by a Minneapolis police officer on June 1, 2020, in New York. (Bryan R. Smith / AFP)
Upcoming events like the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade and New Year's ball drop will not be impacted since the changes aren't slated to go into effect until spring 2027, he said.

NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said in a statement that the restructuring would not "diminish the NYPD’s ability to protect New Yorkers, or that put our officers in a position where they lack the resources necessary to confront a serious threat."

title: Democratic judge under fire for releasing violent offenders calls bail law a ‘direct assault’ on rights
summary: Judge David Carpenter called Alabama’s Aniah’s Law a ‘direct assault’ on constitutional rights, citing defendants’ presumption of innocence.
story: Birmingham Mayor Randall Woodfin tells community that "It’s your time to step up and we need you." (Credit: WBMA)

A Democratic Alabama judge facing mounting scrutiny over past decisions to release violent offenders is criticizing a state law that allows defendants charged with certain violent crimes to be denied bail.

Circuit Court Judge David Carpenter called Alabama’s Aniah’s Law a direct assault on constitutional rights, arguing that defendants should not be held indefinitely based solely on criminal charges, citing the constitutional presumption of innocence.
In a social media post, Carpenter argued that critics of government overreach involving license plate cameras, such as Flock cameras, are not equally concerned about expanded pretrial detention laws.

"Can someone explain to me why the people who are so alarmed that a flock camera might spot their car on a public road, and they call that government overreach, are silent on the fact that voters across the country keep overwhelmingly passing new laws to empower the government to hold you in jail indefinitely on the basis of a charge only," Carpenter said.
THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC?

Damien McDaniel, 22, is connected to more than a dozen murders in the Birmingham, Alabama, area since July 2023, according to city police. Carpenter approved a plea deal for McDaniel before his alleged shooting spree left 18 dead.  (Alabama Department of Corrections / Birmingham Police Department)

"These laws, like Alabama’s Aniah’s Law, are a direct assault on the Constitutional guarantee of the presumption of innocence. But no one is talking about this at all, much less expressing the hysteria associated with having a camera see a license plate," he said.

Although Aniah’s Law was originally passed in 2022, Alabama voters approved a major constitutional amendment this year expanding the law to cover additional offenses. The expansion added attempted murder, solicitation or conspiracy to commit murder, and discharging a firearm or explosives into an occupied dwelling, building or vehicle.
"We are all one accusation away from being a criminal defendant," Carpenter said in a post on Facebook.
WHITE HOUSE CALLS DC POLICIES 'INSANITY' AFTER 19-YEAR-OLD GUNMAN GETS PROBATION IN SHOOTING

Carpenter has faced controversy over several judicial decisions over the years. Local outlet 1819 News reported that he previously described himself online as a "far left, liberal, progressive, democratic socialist."

In April 2023, Carpenter approved a plea deal for Damien McDaniel, who was arrested in 2019 for shooting two people in a car when he was 17 years old, 1819 News reported. After being released from jail, McDaniel allegedly went on a 14-month shooting spree across Alabama, killing 18 people and injuring more than 30 others.
Carpenter approved a plea deal for Damien McDaniel, 22, who was later linked to multiple shootings over 14 months. (Birmingham Police Department / WBRC)

title: Illegal alien accused of attempted murder at large after Rikers release despite ICE detainer: DHS

story: NYC ICE official Kenneth Genalo blasts Mayor Zohran Mamdani and sanctuary policies, warning they force agents into dangerous street arrests and put public safety at risk.

A Guyanese citizen living in the United States illegally remains at large after being released from custody in New York City earlier this month, despite facing multiple violent felony charges and an active federal immigration detainer, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

DHS officials stated that Delon Raymond Jaundoo was arrested in Brooklyn on charges including attempted murder, first- and second-degree assault, criminal use of a firearm, and multiple counts of criminal possession of a loaded weapon.
His prior criminal record also includes an arrest for third-degree assault.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged an immigration detainer for Jaundoo on April 29, which the New York City Department of Correction declined to honor, allowing him to be released from Rikers Island.
MANHUNT UNDERWAY FOR VIOLENT ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO WAS RELEASED UNDER NYC SANCTUARY POLICIES

Delon Raymond Jaundoo, an illegal immigrant from Guyana, has multiple violent crime arrest, including for attempted murder. He remains at large after he was released from Rikers Island Jail in New York City under the city's sanctuary policies, the Department of Homeland Security said. (Department of Homeland Security; Getty Images)

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized New York’s sanctuary policies following the release, arguing that state and local laws prevent cooperation with federal immigration authorities even in cases involving violent offenses.
Jaundoo lawfully entered the country during the Obama administration but overstayed his authorized stay, which expired in January 2015, according to DHS.

"Despite these violent charges, sanctuary politicians in New York refused to honor ICE’s detainer and released this criminal back onto the streets to put more American lives in danger," Mullin said in a statement. "Under Governor Kathy Hochul, New York has become a hotbed of illegal alien crime."
DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani signs executive orders with campaign volunteers during an appearance at Grand Army Plaza in Brooklyn on January 2, 2026, in New York City. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
"The sooner we put an end to these reckless sanctuary policies, the sooner we can all work together to make America safe again," he added.
Jaundoo's release comes amid ongoing restrictions on local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
HOCHUL BOASTS 'I JUST BANNED IT' AS NEW YORK OUTLAWS LOCAL POLICE PARTNERSHIPS WITH ICE

Upon taking office, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani signed an executive order limiting city coordination with ICE, and a state law signed by Gov. Kathy Hochul took effect in August barring local authorities from cooperating with federal immigration officials.

DHS stated that several other illegal immigrants arrested for or convicted of violent crimes, including murder, arson, assault, and rape, have similarly been released from custody under the state's current policies.

"Governor Hochul has been clear: New York State is not and never will be a sanctuary for violent criminals," a spokesperson for Hochul told Fox News Digital. "By law, New York State always notifies federal immigration enforcement of any non-citizen serving a State prison sentence. title: United Airlines says technology issue resolved after ‘widespread system outage’
summary: United Airlines flights were stuck on tarmacs as pilots reported a companywide IT issue preventing takeoff data, days after the nationwide FAA ground stop.
story: Fox News contributor Jonathan Turley joins ‘Special Report’ to describe his firsthand experience aboard a grounded aircraft as a nationwide FAA ground stop disrupts air travel across the country. Turley discusses the uncertainty facing stranded passengers, frustration over limited communication and the challenges travelers face as they await updates on when flights can resume.
United Airlines said Monday it resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, marking another disruption for travelers just days after a nationwide FAA ground stop.

"We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures. While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights," United Media Relations told Fox News Digital.
"There is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue," the airline added.
Earlier Monday, passengers reported being unable to take off, with one saying their flight was returning to the gate because the crew could not obtain performance data needed for departure.
FORMER TOP FAA OFFICIAL WARNS OF 48-HOUR RECOVERY AFTER AGING TECH 'OVERWHELMED' AHEAD OF GROUND STOP
United initially acknowledged a widespread outage in a response to a passenger on X.
"We're aware of the widespread system outage, and our teams are working hard to get things back up and running as soon as possible," United’s official X account wrote in response to a passenger.
The airline apologized and urged travelers to monitor their flight status through the United app or its website. Its response did not identify the cause or provide an estimated restoration time.
One passenger reported being stuck on the tarmac, saying crews could not clear planes for takeoff because they could not connect to a weight system.
Another social media user said their flight was returning to the gate after the pilot announced a company wide IT issue that left the crew "unable to get performance data for takeoff."
"Pilot just announced ALL of United Airlines has a company wide IT issue," the user wrote. "We’re going back to the gate."
Another passenger reported a similar announcement while waiting for departure.
"Waiting to take off, on the runway, and the pilot just said we can’t take off because United is experiencing a system-wide computer outage," the user wrote.
AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS
A United Airlines Boeing 737 MAX aircraft prepares for takeoff at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on July 10, 2025. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)
The X account @theATCapp also posted that it was receiving reports of a systemwide IT outage affecting the airline.
United’s response acknowledged a widespread outage but did not confirm the passengers’ descriptions of the affected systems. The number of flights and airports affected was not immediately clear.
Flight-tracking service Flightradar24 reported that United’s mainline departures were beginning to resume.
"We are seeing mainline departures resuming in the last few minutes," the service posted on X.

At Los Angeles International Airport, Fox News correspondent Max Gorden spoke with several passengers at the United counter who were able to check in for their flights. However, an agent showed Gorden her United mobile device, which appeared to be experiencing technical problems.

The outage comes after a telecommunications failure prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to issue a nationwide ground stop Friday, Nov. 13. The restriction was later lifted, but airlines faced lingering delays and cancellations as they worked to restore their schedules.

Following Friday’s ground stop, United CEO Scott Kirby praised the FAA’s decision to halt flights and thanked employees and customers for their patience. He also called for better technology and full staffing to help prevent future outages.

Scott Kirby, chief executive officer at United Airlines Holdings Inc., during a Bloomberg Television interview at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) in Newark, New Jersey, US, on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026.  (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Kirby said he had spoken directly with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and aviation leaders from both parties in Congress about the impact on United’s passengers and employees.
"This moment must be a call to action," Kirby said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital.
United Airlines planes sit parked at the gate at San Francisco International Airport on April 24, 2025, in San Francisco, California. (Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)
"It is critical for safety, our passengers, and our economy that we fix our nation’s Air Traffic Control system now."
Kirby said lawmakers from both parties were committed to modernizing the system while holding the FAA accountable.

title: TIMELINE: America hits a tech wall as outages cripple email, ground flights and disrupt major banks
summary: America’s tech troubles stretched into a sixth day as Apple, the National Weather Service and NSA reported disruptions following Microsoft, FAA, Workday and Chase issues.
story: LendingTree analyst Matt Schulz warns customers to watch for scammers exploiting confusion around reported Chase outages. His advice: verify updates directly with your bank and never share personal information with unsolicited callers or messages.

America’s technology troubles stretched into a sixth day Tuesday as Apple services experienced disruptions and the National Weather Service and National Security Agency reported technical problems during routine maintenance.

Apple’s status page showed issues affecting the App Store, Apple Music and AppleCare before listing the App Store and Apple Music as restored. The National Weather Service said its technical problems had been resolved. The NSA said some internal systems were affected but its mission-critical capabilities remained fully operational.
The latest issues followed disruptions at Microsoft, Workday and JPMorgan Chase, along with a nationwide FAA ground stop that upended air travel.
PERPETUAL PARALYSIS: WHY EVERYTHING IS GRINDING TO A HALT
Chase confirmed to Fox News Monday evening that transactions were processing normally. Bank of America said its systems had operated normally throughout the day.
Here is a timeline of the technology turmoil:
Chase Bank in Manhattan, New York City on July 16th, 2024. (Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
4 CRITICAL TRAVEL ISSUES FOR THOSE DELAYED AND DISRUPTED BY FAA NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP
A widespread Microsoft 365 outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and other services, leaving users struggling to access email and other functions.

The incident began Thursday and lasted nearly 24 hours, with service restored Friday morning, according to Microsoft’s preliminary incident report. Email suffered the most significant disruption, while the impact on other services varied.
Microsoft suffered a major outage that lasted nearly 24 hours. (Microsoft)
Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna attributed the failure to a combination of a previously undetected software defect, increased traffic and reduced server capacity.
Microsoft says more than 430 million people use its Microsoft 365 apps. That figure represents the platform’s user base, rather than a confirmed tally of people affected.
A person looks at a departures board showing delays and cancellations at LaGuardia airport on November 13, 2026 in the Queens borough of New York City. (Adam Gray/Getty Images)
The FAA halted departures nationwide for nearly five hours Friday after technical problems destabilized aircraft communications and radar feeds.
The disruption began around 3:30 p.m. Eastern, with air traffic resuming at 8:15 p.m., according to the agency.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the problems began when contractor L3Harris Technologies Inc. was replacing old copper wiring with fiber wiring in the air traffic control system, causing a system overload.
BUTTIGIEG TAKES SWIPE AT TRUMP ADMINISTRATION AMID FAA FLIGHT CHAOS

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy speaks during a press briefing at Department of Transportation headquarters on Nov. 14, 2026, in Washington, D.C. The briefing followed a nationwide communications outage that grounded flights across the United States the previous day. (Aaron Schwartz / AFP via Getty Images)
The work led to intermittent communications and radar gaps. Duffy said officials were investigating whether contractor incompetence or a faulty router was responsible.
"Our contractor didn’t meet the moment or the equipment didn’t meet the moment," Duffy said.
NBA AND NHL TEAMS BATTLE DELAYS AS NATIONWIDE FAA GROUND STOP DISRUPTS WEEKEND SPORTS TRAVEL
Some radio frequencies and radar feeds remained operational, and every aircraft landed safely, according to the FAA.
Operators canceled approximately 12,462 flights Friday, including 9,082 by major airlines, the FAA said, while cautioning that not all cancellations were directly caused by the ground stop.
UPDATED START TIMES FOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL GAMES AFFECTED BY FAA GROUND STOP, BROKEN DOWN BY CONFERENCE
The agency said it had no indication of a cyberattack.
Workday, whose payroll and human resources software is used by millions of employees, experienced a widespread outage Friday, a day after Microsoft’s disruption.

The platform manages services for about 11,500 companies, including Walmart, Target, Netflix, Southwest Airlines and PNC Bank. Its clients also include government agencies and NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, though not all customers reported outages.
"Workday is currently unavailable," a message shown to users said. "We are experiencing a service interruption. Your service will be restored as quickly as possible."
Outage-tracking website Downdetector recorded a spike of nearly 3,000 reports shortly after 5 p.m. Friday.

"Some of our customers are experiencing a service disruption, and we’re working urgently to investigate and resolve the issue," a Workday spokesperson told Fox News. "We sincerely apologize for the challenges this is causing impacted customers."
Customers at Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo reported online banking difficulties Monday, adding banking to the list of everyday services hit by technology trouble.

Chase initially said some transactions were taking longer than usual but customers retained access to their accounts and money. The bank later confirmed to Fox News that transactions were processing normally.
The incident was traced to a software release JPMorgan Chase rolled out earlier Monday that affected a subset of its systems. There was no indication of malicious or external cyber activity.
The impact was limited to JPMorgan Chase and transactions at other financial institutions in which JPMorgan Chase was a party.
Bank branch as they experience disruptions due to the banking technology outage.  (Ava Palschakov for Fox News Digital)
JPMorgan Chase initially said systems were coming back online and the incident was not malicious.

"Bank of America systems have been operating normally today. Clients experiencing delays with other providers may wish to contact them directly for the latest information," Bank of America said in a statement.
The extent and causes of the reported problems at the other banks were not immediately clear.
Zelle told FOX Business its payment network was operating normally, but problems at financial institutions could be delaying payments for some customers.

"Zelle is not down. Zelle is operating as it should," the company said. "Consumers use Zelle through participating banks and credit unions, which manage their accounts and hold their funds. Consumers do not have a separate Zelle account, and Zelle does not hold consumer funds."
"An issue at the financial institutions may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers. Please contact them directly," Zelle added.
Routine network maintenance caused technical problems for some users of National Weather Service websites and data services Tuesday morning, the agency said.
The disruption lasted from 11:05 a.m. to 11:45 a.m. Eastern and has been resolved. NOAA Weather Radio and NOAAPort were not affected.
"As always, NWS advises everyone to have multiple ways of receiving critical, time-sensitive warnings," the agency said in a statement.
Apple's iCloud — where millions of users store photos, documents and other personal data — is seeing a spike in user-reported login issues Tuesday, according to outage tracker Downdetector.
The page later listed the App Store and Apple Music as back online as service statuses continued to change.
Customers at Apple's Fifth Avenue store in New York City on Sept. 18, 2026.  (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Users also reported Apple Pay problems on outage-tracking website Downdetector, though Apple’s status page did not list an Apple Pay issue at the time.
Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.
The National Security Agency said scheduled routine maintenance temporarily degraded some internal systems Tuesday, while its mission-critical capabilities remained fully operational.

"The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance. While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues," the agency said in a statement.
"NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events," the agency added.

SAN FRANCISCO HOME WITH HISTORY OF SQUATTERS UNDER CONTRACT FOR $1.3 MILLION

title: Lindsay Clancy to be retried for murder in killing of three children
summary: Lindsay Clancy's murder retrial in the strangling deaths of her three children is set for March 29 after her first trial ended with a deadlocked jury.
story: Massachusetts Judge William Sullivan denies Lindsay Clancy's motion for acquittal, pushing the high-profile murder case toward a November 2 hearing.
A Massachusetts judge set March 29 as the start date for Lindsay Clancy's retrial on murder charges in the strangling deaths of her three young children.

The former nurse's first trial ended on Sept. 4 with a jury deadlocked 11-1, with only a single juror voting to find her guilty of murder. The others sided with her defense, which argued that she should not be found criminally responsible due to mental illness.

Judge William Sullivan repeatedly told the parties to pick a date in March or April. Prosecutors had wanted May at the start and later pushed for the end of April. Sullivan ultimately chose the late March date.
LINDSAY CLANCY PROSECUTORS FACE DILEMMA: RETRIAL OR PLEA DEAL IN CASE INVOLVING 3 STRANGLED CHILDREN

Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Pool Photo by Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)
"You've all done retrials, and generally, the sooner it is the case is retried, the better it is for all parties," he said.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Although prosecutors did not specifically address whether they intend to seek the same charges, Clancy's defense lawyer, Kevin Reddington, said he anticipated that they plan to move forward on the same counts of first-degree murder.

Lesser charges could open the door for a plea deal or even a bench trial, according to legal experts.

Reddington told Fox News' Bryan Llenas in September that if prosecutors reduced the top charge to second-degree murder, he would opt for a bench trial — one without jurors — in the hope that she receives probation as punishment.

Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
GOT A TIP?

"I would like to see [Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz] reduce it to a second-degree so we could possibly waive a jury and try the case before a judge," he said. "I would see Tim determine that the case should not go forward and dismiss it, or in the alternative fashion, something where Lindsay gets the mental, physical help that she needs rather than criminal prosecution — because I would not ever, ever in a million years have that woman go to Framingham State Prison."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Jack Lu, a retired Massachusetts judge and law professor, said a bench trial would use significantly fewer resources than a second jury trial. Prosecutors could seek second-degree murder charges if they decide her mental illness prevented her from forming the intent required for first-degree murder, he said.
Because of Sullivan's looming retirement, any delays could force the second trial to be held in front of a new judge.

"Perhaps this will be the unusual murder trial that goes off without a hitch," he told Fox News Digital. "For example, have the attorneys double-checked and locked in the availability of experts? This could delay the trial."
He also questioned whether Clancy's retrial should take priority over other cases in the same court.
"My answer: It should not," he said Monday.

Patrick Clancy exits Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., Monday, July27, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
"It appears to be pushing aside older murder trials," Lu said. "I agree with the prosecutor on this point: ‘It is unfair to them.’ Them is victims and defendants in other murder cases."
Assistant Plymouth County District Attorney Jennifer Sprague had raised other cases slated for trial in her argument for a May trial date, but Sullivan set it for March over her objection.

On Jan. 24, 2023, Clancy's ex-husband Patrick Clancy came home to find her critically injured in their backyard and their three young children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — strangled to death inside.
LINDSAY CLANCY DEFENSE FILES MOTION TO DISMISS UNDER DOUBLE JEOPARDY GROUNDS, WITH FOCUS ON HOLDOUT JUROR

Prosecutors said Clancy attempted to take her own life after killing the children while her husband was out doing errands. Her injuries left her paralyzed. She's been held at a Massachusetts hospital as her case plays out.

title: Trump border crackdown drives encounters to record October low as zero-release streak hits 18 months, DHS says
summary: Border Patrol recorded just 8,288 southwest border apprehensions in October, marking a stunning 95% drop from the Biden administration's average.
story: Rep. Pat Fallon sounds the alarm on lawmakers potentially softening their stance on immigration policy and border security. Fallon contrasts the record high of over 200,000 illegal crossings per month under former President Joe Biden with the successful enforcement strategies implemented by President Donald Trump. Fallon emphasizes that protecting citizens requires a strong presidential will rather than congressional action.

Border Patrol agents caught fewer illegal immigrants at the southwest border in all of October than they did in just five days of the same month under former President Joe Biden in 2024, according to new federal figures.

The sharp drop comes as the Trump administration reports 18 straight months of zero releases at the border and the lowest nationwide encounter total ever recorded for the opening month of a fiscal year.
"President Trump unleashed the full strength of DHS to secure the border and enforce the law," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said. "The results speak for themselves."
TRUMP DHS HITS 16 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH 0 RELEASES AT THE BORDER

U.S. Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations officers conduct a helicopter demonstration of their rapid response capabilities during a joint exercise at the border between El Paso, Texas, and Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua, Mexico, on Aug. 13, 2026. (Herika Martinez/AFP via Getty Images)
"Under President Trump’s leadership, we will continue to deliver the most secure border in American history and save American lives," Mullin added.

Border Patrol recorded 8,288 apprehensions along the southwest border in October, down 95% from the Biden administration’s monthly average and 97% from its December 2023 peak, according to the Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Customs and Border Protection.
TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94%
A construction vehicle builds the border wall near Sunland Park, New Mexico, in 2026. (Christian Torres/Getty Images)

The numbers stand in sharp contrast to the surge retired Yuma Sector Border Patrol Chief Chris Clem described in an October interview with Fox News Digital, when he recalled overwhelmed agents and migrants spilling into surrounding communities.

"They just started walking through the agriculture fields. They started running through town," Clem said, recalling December 2021. "They started going to the food bank. They started knocking on people’s doors at all hours of the night."
CBS REPORT MARVELS AT ONCE-CHAOTIC SOUTHERN BORDER CROSSING HAS GONE QUIET UNDER TRUMP CRACKDOWN

In Yuma alone, Clem said daily arrivals climbed from roughly 25 in December 2020 to more than 1,000 a year later. During one particularly difficult three-day stretch in December 2021, daily arrivals approached 1,500, he said.
"The agents, their heads were in the right place. They knew they had to do the job," Clem said. "But when you’re outnumbered, literally 100 to one, it’s very difficult."
DHS TOUTS MILLIONS OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT DEPARTURES AS BORDER CROSSINGS DROP 94% UNDER TRUMP
U.S. Border Patrol agent Nicole Ballistrea watches over the U.S.-Mexico border fence in Nogales, Arizona. (John Moore/Getty Images)
The latest southwest border apprehension total fell 7% from September, carrying the decline into the first month of fiscal year 2027.
Nationwide, CBP recorded 27,890 encounters in October, also down 7% from September. That was the lowest October total on record and the lowest for any month since February, the agencies said.
TRUMP HITS DRAMATIC MILESTONE IN MASSIVE DEPARTURE FROM BIDEN BORDER PLAN: 'WHAT A DIFFERENCE'

The new figures follow preliminary DHS data showing 98,708 southwest border apprehensions for all of fiscal year 2026, roughly 95% below the Biden administration’s annual average of more than 1.8 million.
Clem credited stronger border enforcement and the prospect of deportation with changing the calculation for people considering crossing illegally.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

A U.S. Border Patrol checkpoint on Interstate 19, about 20 miles north of the Mexican border. Agents stop all northbound traffic, looking for undocumented immigrants and drug smugglers. Dogs help in the search. (Jim West/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)
"They know that they’re not gonna be processed and released, which was the status quo under the Biden-Harris administration," he told Fox News Digital in the October interview.
He said enforcement inside the country reinforced that message by making clear that getting past Border Patrol did not eliminate the possibility of arrest and removal.
ICE ARRESTS MORE THAN 100 ALLEGED GANG MEMBERS IN SINGLE WEEK, INCLUDING VIOLENT MS-13, TDA SUSPECTS: DHS
"When you combine the strong border posture, as well as the strong and robust interior enforcement, it’s a recipe for success," Clem said.
CBP Commissioner Rodney S. Scott credited Trump and Mullin with giving the agency an "unprecedented level of control over our borders."
MULLIN TELLS RUTHLESS PODCAST THAT THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS APPREHENDED 2,210 TERRORISTS
Secretary Markwayne Mullin shakes hands with President Donald Trump, left, after his swearing in. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)
"We know more about who and what is entering our homeland than at any time in our nation’s history," Scott said in the latest announcement.
"America is safer because we are enforcing the rule of law, keeping threats out of our communities and putting the security of the American people first," he added.
The decline in border apprehensions came as CBP reported a jump in the weight of drugs seized nationwide.

Seizures of cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin, fentanyl and marijuana collectively rose 44% from September, according to the agencies. Officers and agents seized 14,745 pounds of methamphetamine and 9,032 pounds of cocaine in October, increases of 59% and 60%, respectively.
The release did not include a separate October total for fentanyl.
Still, Clem cautioned in October that lower apprehension numbers did not eliminate threats from smugglers or people trying to evade detection.
"There are always gonna be that risk where somebody does sneak through. Who is that person?" he said.
"We have an immigration issue we need to address," Clem said. "We need to find a way to retain and recruit those that are here, that are foreign nationals that want to contribute."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"But none of that should matter when it comes down to securing the border," he added. "We should always be looking at keeping America safe."
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Person of interest being questioned by FBI in Illinois ethanol plant bomb investigation
summary: FBI Springfield, Illinois, is leading the manhunt after a credible explosive device was found at BioUrja Renewables in Peoria, sparking evacuations.
story: The ‘Big Weekend Show’ panel discusses a bomb found at an ethanol plant in Illinois and the ongoing investigation.
A person of interest is being questioned Monday in an investigation into who left a bomb near an ethanol facility in Peoria, Illinois, a police spokesperson confirmed to Fox News.
The FBI, whose Springfield, Illinois, office is leading the ongoing investigation, confirmed "law enforcement activity" in Peoria County but did not get specific on the questioning.
Peoria police had previously said a "person of interest has been taken into custody," but later adjusted that statement.
Peoria police redirected all further comment to the FBI Springfield Field Office.
"The Peoria Police Department has no further comment at this time," spokesperson Semone Roth said.
BOMB FOUND AT PEORIA ETHANOL PLANT PROMPTS EVACUATIONS

Federal investigators have taken over the probe and manhunt for someone who left a "credible threat" and called in a bomb scare at a sprawling Illinois ethanol plant that spans 44½ football fields. (FBI Springfield Office)

The explosive device found at BioUrja Renewables on Friday led to evacuations within a one-mile "blast radius" and triggered nearly a 24-hour emergency response. A large facility the size of 44½ football fields and a large area that was evacuated suggested a potentially major threat to public safety.

"I can just tell you it was deemed a credible threat," Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon told reporters at a briefing Saturday, noting that forensic testing is still underway to determine the exact composition of the device. "There's an extensive criminal investigation going on."
Dixon declined to call the device a "bomb" despite the facility reporting to police it had received a bomb threat.

Authorities warned that because the facility houses large quantities of ethanol and other highly combustible chemicals, an ignition could have triggered a massive explosion far larger than the device itself.
IED NEAR ALABAMA RESERVOIR DETONATED AFTER OFFICIALS WARN OF 'UNPRECEDENTED' CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE THREAT

FBI Special Agent Ryan Presley said the investigation remains in its preliminary stages, declining to release further details about a potential motive or suspect. A Sunday morning news conference held by the Springfield office was postponed until at least Monday.

"While the area has been cleared and no additional suspicious devices have been located, the FBI encourages the public to remain alert and share any relevant information they may have," Springfield FBI posted Saturday to X.

"We will work tirelessly to identify the individual responsible and bring them to justice," Presley added, noting the FBI has provided bomb technicians, investigative and intelligence resources to local authorities before taking over the lead of the investigation.
WAVE OF SCHOOL BOMB THREATS ROCKS KENTUCKY AMID SUSPECTED ROBOCALL SCHEME, POLICE SAY
The incident began Friday afternoon when workers at the Peoria plant reported a bomb threat they received to police. Roughly an hour later, crews located a suspicious package near the facility.

Peoria Mayor Rita Ali warned of a potentially catastrophic event because, she told WMBD-TV, BioUrja is "a plant that has ethanol and highly combustible types of chemicals, and so that’s what alarms us."

By Saturday afternoon, officials from the Peoria Police Department, the FBI and the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives completed their search of the facility and confirmed no other items of concern were found. Bomb technicians rendered it safe, Peoria police said.

The evacuation order was lifted Saturday, almost a full day after the device was discovered Friday close to the ethanol plant in Peoria, a city of about 110,000 people, about 150 miles southwest of Chicago. Bomb technicians rendered it safe, Peoria police said.
CAR LOADED WITH EXPLOSIVES SLAMS INTO LAVISH PORTLAND SOCIAL CLUB, BOMB SQUAD STILL PULLING OUT LIVE DEVICES
"We understand that this is a disruptive process for our residents and guests," Dixon said. "We’re asking for the public’s patience while we work to make this area safe."
No injuries were reported, and no arrests have been made.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ALLEGEDLY MADE BOMB THREAT ON FLIGHT, DHS SAYS

"#FBISpringfield is now leading the investigation following the identification of an explosive device found at BioUrja Renewables on Friday, Nov. 13," the Saturday X post began. "While the area has been cleared and no additional suspicious devices have been located, the FBI encourages the public to remain alert and share any relevant information they may have related to this ongoing situation by immediately calling 9-1-1, 1-800-CALL-FBI, or online at http:// tips.fbi.gov.

"Tipsters may elect to remain anonymous," it added. "The FBI continues to work closely with local, state, and federal law enforcement partners, to include @ATFHQ, @ILSecOfState, @ILStatePolice, the Peoria County Sheriff’s Office, Peoria Fire Department, and @peoria_police, to identify the individual(s) responsible and will hold them fully accountable under the law. All releasable investigative updates will be shared via official FBI Springfield social channels."

Because the BioUrja Renewables plant sits directly on the banks of the Illinois River, the one-mile evacuation zone extended across the waterway. Coast Guard Capt. Brandy Parker confirmed the agency established a safety perimeter blocking all vessel traffic between mile markers 160 and 164 while bomb technicians rendered the device safe and searched the facility.

The Illinois River, a major tributary of the Mississippi, is a major commercial shipping corridor. The Coast Guard is responsible for securing inland navigable waterways and waterfront industrial facilities against terrorism, sabotage and hazardous material spills — especially given the catastrophic environmental and safety risks if an explosion had ignited the plant's ethanol reserves.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Parker serves as the sector commander for U.S. Coast Guard Sector Upper Mississippi River. The safety shutdown came the same weekend Coast Guard crews far south in Sector New Orleans were forced to close a stretch of the lower Mississippi River after the asphalt tanker Atlantic Asphalt collided with a docked cruise ship carrying 129 passengers near the Port of New Orleans.
Fox News' Janelle Benham, The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Mamdani guts elite NYPD tactical unit, backs 'civilian-led approach' to responding to protests
summary: Zohran Mamdani disbands the NYPD Strategic Response Group and unveils a civilian-led dialogue team to handle New York City protest response.
story: NYC ICE official Kenneth Genalo blasts Mayor Zohran Mamdani and sanctuary policies, warning they force agents into dangerous street arrests and put public safety at risk.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the disbanding of the NYPD's Strategic Response Group (SRG) on Monday, saying the city will now pursue a "civilian-led approach" to responding to protests.

Mamdani made the announcement alongside Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, stating that the SRG's counterterrorism functions will be folded into an existing command, while a brand-new organization will now lead protest response, the Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD).

The CDDD, which will lie within the Mayor's Office of Community Safety, will work to "improve the NYPD's protest response" via a specialized "dialogue team," known as the First Amendment Support Team (FAST), they said.

"The CDDD will not have weapons or arrest powers. FAST will consist of 30 uniformed officers trained in communication and de-escalation. The NYPD will also establish a new Patrol Support Division (PSD), a unit within the NYPD’s Patrol Services Bureau, with vetted officers who will spend most of their time on patrol-related duties and receive specialized crowd management training to support responses to demonstrations," the mayor's office said in a statement.
NYC MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI SAYS HE WON'T FIRE NYPD COMMISSIONER JESSICA TISCH DESPITE SOCIALIST PRESSURE
The NYPD Strategic Response Group (SRG) monitors a crowd outside 26 Federal Plaza on Oct. 21, 2025 in New York City. (Photo by Adam Gray/Getty Images)

"During our campaign, I promised New Yorkers that we would disband the Strategic Response Group and separate counterterrorism from protest response, and today we are delivering on that promise," Mamdani said in a statement.
MINNEAPOLIS PROGRESSIVES TURN ON GEORGE FLOYD-ERA PUBLIC SAFETY OVERHAUL, PUSH TO DISMANTLE OFFICE
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch speak at a Sunday morning news conference after a spate of weekend shootings in Brooklyn. (Kyle Mazza/Anadolu)

"New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat. We are establishing a new, civilian-led approach that prioritizes dialogue, engagement and de-escalation," he added.

The reforms also impose new restrictions on the tools police are allowed to use when responding to protests, including codified bans on kettling, long guns and tear gas. Pepper spray will also not be used as a crowd management tool, and "long-range acoustic devices" will be limited to 90 decibels.
MAMDANI, NYPD GIVE SECURITY UPDATE AHEAD OF JEWISH HIGH HOLY DAYS, 9/11 25TH ANNIVERSARY

NYPD officers detain a demonstrator during a protest amid a two-week ceasefire in the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran, along Third Avenue in the Midtown area of New York City on April 13, 2026. (Shannon Stapleton/Reuters)

Under the previous structure, the NYPD said the SRG responded to citywide mobilizations, civil disorders and major events and was a "critical asset" during parades, protests and the papal visit. SRG personnel were "also deployed to areas requiring an increased police presence due to increased crime or other conditions" and "mobilizes for shootings, bank robberies, missing persons, demonstrations, or other significant incidents," according to the department.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Tisch noted at a March budget hearing that the SRG did not typically deal with peaceful protests, but was deployed for protests that involved criminal activity. She also noted that in 2025, the NYPD facilitated 4,255 protests and the SRG was available at 245 of them, or roughly 6%.
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: Young paraglider dies after reported emergency sends him crashing into field during Illinois flight
summary: Officials are investigating a fatal paragliding incident involving a 21-year-old man from a Chicago suburb who shared his aerial adventures and daring stunts online.
story: Giovanni Lopez’s death remains under investigation as officials await an autopsy to determine the cause and manner of death.(Giovanni Lopez/Facebook)
An Illinois paraglider died in a weekend crash after reportedly experiencing an emergency mid-flight.
Officials on Saturday identified the victim as Giovanni Lopez, 21, of Woodridge, a southwest suburb of Chicago.
Lopez frequently documented his paragliding adventures and daring aerial maneuvers on social media.
The Kendall County Coroner’s Office said it was notified around 3:40 p.m. Saturday of a possible fatality in Plainfield, an area dotted with farm fields southwest of Chicago.
CLIMBER STRANDED ON 6-INCH LEDGE AT 11,000 FEET AS 46 MPH WINDS GROUND RESCUE HELICOPTER
Giovanni Lopez, 21, died in a paragliding incident in Plainfield, Illinois, after a reported midair emergency. (Giovanni Lopez/Facebook)
"The Kendall County Coroner’s Office was notified of a possible fatality related to a paragliding incident in the area of Ridge Road and 127th Street in Plainfield, Illinois," the office said.
Officials did not disclose the exact circumstances that led to Lopez’s death.
NBC Chicago reported that Lopez encountered an emergency while paragliding.
HIKER IDENTIFIED, POPULAR TRAIL CLOSED AFTER DEADLY FALL AT UTAH'S ZION NATIONAL PARK
Giovanni Lopez frequently shared videos of his paragliding adventures and daring aerial stunts on social media. (Giovanni Lopez/Facebook)
Witnesses reportedly rushed to Lopez's aid and attempted to help him until paramedics arrived and continued lifesaving efforts, the outlet said.
Upon arrival, coroner’s deputies pronounced Lopez dead at the scene.
Officials said the cause and manner of death will be determined following a forensic autopsy.
The incident remains under investigation by the Plainfield Police Department and the Kendall County Coroner's Office.
Giovanni Lopez wears a motorized propeller unit on his back as part of his paragliding equipment. (Giovanni Lopez/Facebook)

Additional agencies assisted in the investigation, including the Oswego Fire Protection District and the Kendall County Sheriff's Office.

title: NTSB details warning whistles and emergency orders before tanker collision capsized New Orleans riverboat
summary: NTSB investigators detail warning whistles and emergency orders captured on the tanker's voyage recorder before the New Orleans riverboat collision.
story: NTSB investigators detail a steering problem, warning whistles and emergency anchor orders in the minutes before the Atlantic Asphalt struck the docked American Heritage in New Orleans. (Credit: WVUE)

A tanker suffered a steering problem about two minutes before slamming into a docked New Orleans riverboat Friday, federal investigators said Sunday, detailing warning whistles, calls for help and emergency orders before the collision.

The Atlantic Asphalt was heading upriver near the Crescent City Connection Bridge at about 12:26 p.m. when its rudder remained turned to the right, sending the ship toward the Mississippi River’s east bank, National Transportation Safety Board senior marine accident investigator Bart Barnum said.
The tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage at about 12:28 p.m. The riverboat capsized in about 22 minutes, according to preliminary information presented by the NTSB.
NEW ORLEANS BOAT CRASH CALLED ‘MIRACLE ON THE MISSISSIPPI’ AS EVERYONE IS ACCOUNTED FOR, OFFICIALS SAY
NTSB team surveying the wreckage. (NTSB)
Investigators downloaded more than nine hours of data from the tanker’s voyage data recorder, including bridge audio, rudder angle, engine RPM, course and speed.

The recordings captured sounds consistent with the ship’s whistle, warnings and requests for assistance over its marine radio, commands to deploy anchors and emergency shiphandling orders, Barnum said.
11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP
Officials described the steering problem as a "steering casualty," but cautioned that the term does not establish what went wrong.
"It could be many different things. That is something that we are investigating very closely," Barnum said.
AT LEAST 6 PEOPLE INJURED AFTER BOSTON DUCK BOAT OVERTURNS NEAR ENTRANCE TO POPULAR TOURIST ATTRACTION
Tugboats surround the Atlantic Asphalt tanker in New Orleans following its collision with the docked American Heritage river cruiser on Nov. 13, 2026. (Kat Ramirez for Fox News Digital)

NTSB board member John DeLeeuw said investigators have data on the tanker’s speed but are still analyzing it before releasing it publicly. Video showed anchors were down, but investigators are still determining which ones were deployed and how far, he said.

The findings follow a frantic rescue effort that officials said left everyone aboard the American Heritage alive. Roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River, while responders evacuated more than 80 before the vessel overturned, Port of New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll said Saturday.
TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED
"This is a miracle. It is a literal miracle on the Mississippi," Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said Friday.
Eight people remained hospitalized Saturday, including two in serious condition. The other six were stable, officials said.
FBI INVESTIGATES SUSPECTED HOMICIDE ABOARD MSC SEASCAPE CRUISE SHIP AFTER SUDDEN RETURN TO TEXAS
The NTSB said Sunday that 140 passengers and 50 crew members were aboard the riverboat, a total of 190.
New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno also said the American Heritage’s captain was injured but stayed aboard until passengers and crew were accounted for, becoming the last person to leave.
MOM LOSES GRIP ON DAUGHTER AS PASSENGER FERRY CAPSIZES WITH 20 PEOPLE STILL MISSING
"Every moment of the critical time [Friday], he did not want to leave his ship," Moreno said Saturday.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said Saturday that crews were preparing to remove 16,000 gallons of fuel before salvage operations, warning that removing the capsized vessel could take weeks. DeLeeuw said Sunday that divers had been in the water, with salvage work overseen by the Coast Guard and salvage companies.
UNLICENSED NYC BOAT OPERATOR ALLEGEDLY IGNORED SAFETY WARNINGS BEFORE MOTHER, BABY DIED IN CAPSIZING: FEDS
Port of New Orleans collision map. (Google Maps)
Interviews with American Heritage crew members were underway Sunday. Interviews with the Atlantic Asphalt’s crew were scheduled to begin Monday and continue through the week, Barnum said.

The NTSB expects to release a preliminary report within about 30 days. Sunday’s briefing was its last planned on-site news conference, DeLeeuw said, with further updates to be posted online.

title: Europe assassination scheme emerges as Iran denies DC 'dirty bomb' plot amid Trump warning
summary: President Donald Trump warned Iran would pay a price like no other as Tehran's deputy foreign minister called the chemical weapons report a "shameful lie."
story: President Donald Trump warned Iran on Monday that it would face unprecedented retaliation if it were to carry out an attack on Washington, D.C.

Iran on Tuesday slammed allegations that it was plotting a chemical weapons attack in Washington, D.C., calling the claims a "shameful lie" within hours of President Donald Trump warning that Tehran would face unprecedented retaliation if it ever targeted the nation's capital.

Tehran's denial followed a CNN report that U.S. intelligence agencies had uncovered Iranian plans for potential attacks on senior administration officials, including the possible use of chemical weapons or a radioactive "dirty bomb."

The allegations also emerged amid reports of a separate Iranian-linked assassination plot targeting an Israeli executive in Greece and with Israeli security officials believing Tehran aims to target Israelis overseas as the war continues, according to news outlet Ynet Global.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi immediately rejected the allegations in a post on X, invoking Iran's history as a victim of chemical warfare.
TRUMP WARNS US WOULD 'DECIMATE AND DESTROY' IRAN OVER ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT
President Donald Trump has repeatedly alluded to Iranian threats on his life this week. (Jonathan Ernst/Alkis Konstantinidis/Reuters)
"CNN's claim that Iran plans to use chemical weapons in Washington is a shameful lie and a distortion of history," Gharibabadi wrote.
Trump was asked by reporters Tuesday during the first leg of his trip across Asia about the alleged plot against administration officials and if there was an imminent threat to D.C.
"Well, if there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before," Trump said.
"I hope it's not, but ... we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy. But this is why they can't have a nuclear weapon, by the way, in case people had any questions."
SENIOR US OFFICIAL UNDERCUTS CNN'S ALARMING IRAN ‘DIRTY BOMB’ REPORT: ‘IT’S NOT NEW'

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi rejected the allegations of a dirty bomb plot in a post on X. (Askin Kiyagan/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images, File)
"Iran is one of the biggest victims of chemical weapons; victims who were targeted with these inhumane weapons with the support of today's accusers, especially the United States," he added.
"The truth must not become a casualty of the propaganda war," Gharibabadi warned.
TRUMP ADMIN THREATENS IRAN WITH 'CONSEQUENCES' AS ALLIES CONVENE AMID THREATS OF POST-ELECTION ESCALATION

CNN reported, citing seven officials familiar with the intelligence, that American agencies had detected Iranian efforts to develop potential attack options against senior administration officials in Washington.
White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said the administration was monitoring potential threats, but that "at this time, there are no credible threats to the homeland."
IRAN COULD MOVE SHADOW WAR IN A DANGEROUS DIRECTION, EXPERTS WARN ON BACK OF TWO POSSIBLE TERROR ATTACKS

Israeli intelligence reportedly helped foil a separate alleged Iranian-linked assassination plot Tuesday targeting an Israeli executive in Greece, leading to five arrests in Greece and North Macedonia. (Robert Atanasovski/AFP via Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Israeli intelligence reportedly helped foil a separate alleged Iranian-linked assassination plot Tuesday targeting an Israeli executive in Greece, leading to five arrests in Greece and North Macedonia, according to Ynet.
Citing sources, the outlet reported that Mossad gave intelligence to Greek and North Macedonian authorities as part of a joint effort to disrupt the plot.
North Macedonia's National Security Agency announced that authorities had uncovered the plan, with one North Macedonian national arrested in Greece last Thursday and extradited to his home country.
Four others were said to have been detained in Skopje, North Macedonia.

The alleged plot was directed by Iranian national Edris Jahangiri Mavaneh, whom the agency linked to people associated with Iranian intelligence and security services, including alleged drug trafficker Naji Sharifi Zindashti, according to Ynet.
IRAN TRIED TO ASSASSINATE ONE OF NETANYAHU'S SONS, PRIME MINISTER SAYS

Israeli security officials said Tehran considers its war with Israel as unresolved and is looking for opportunities to retaliate through attacks beyond the Middle East region. (Photo by Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Zindashti is also wanted by the FBI for operating a network that targets Iranian activists and dissidents abroad.
According to the bureau, Zindashti used encrypted, Internet-based messaging applications to hire criminal elements within North America and to murder two individuals who fled Iran.
Greek outlet Kathimerini meanwhile, also reported that the suspects allegedly planned to assassinate a senior Israeli executive working for a company operating in Greece.

Investigators seized weapons, ammunition, handwritten notes and a map, according to the report.
North Macedonia's security agency said investigators also uncovered secret meetings involving suspects in several countries, including Iran.
According to Ynet, Israeli security officials said Tehran considers its war with Israel as unresolved and is looking for opportunities to retaliate through attacks beyond the Middle East region.

title: US carries out self-defense strike on IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island
summary: U.S. jets struck an IRGC missile site on Iran’s Qeshm Island Tuesday in self-defense, officials told Fox News.
story: President Donald Trump warned Iran on Monday that it would face unprecedented retaliation if it were to carry out an attack on Washington, D.C.

American fighter aircraft carried out a self-defense airstrike on an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island, Iran, on Tuesday, two U.S. military officials confirmed to Fox News.
"Earlier today, U.S. fighter aircraft used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defense.

"The strike was in response to IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets. U.S. Central Command remains highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region," an official said in a statement.
The strikes came hours after Tehran claimed it targeted a U.S. radar system at the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain.
IRAN’S DRONE HUNT ESCALATES AS TEHRAN TARGETS US SPY TECH TO EXPOSE BATTLEFIELD SECRETS
Commercial vessels are seen anchored between Iran's Qeshm and Larak islands amid disruptions to maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran. (Fatemeh Bahrami/Anadolu via Getty Images, File)

In a statement, the IRGC claimed its operation was in response to violations of Iran's airspace by U.S. drones and said the action was taken to counter "hostile U.S. movements in the region," according to the semi-official, state-sponsored Mehr News Agency.
CENTCOM said later the Iranian attack drones were all intercepted.

"Multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC today towards Bahrain were intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel," the command said in a post shared on X.
Qatar also went on to condemn Iran's ongoing attacks on Bahrain on Tuesday, calling them a violation of Bahraini sovereignty.

"The Ministry underscores that the continuation of these attacks constitutes a grave escalation that threatens regional security and stability and undermines diplomatic efforts aimed at easing tensions," it said in a statement on X.

Qatar also described the Iranian attacks as a "flagrant" violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness, warning that their continuation marked a serious escalation and undermined diplomatic efforts to defuse regional tensions.

The latest attacks also followed a wave of Iranian aerial strikes repelled by Bahrain on Sunday, during which the IRGC claimed to have targeted a radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base with another six drones.
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.
