title: Gas geyser and noxious odor from L.A. area landfill prompts public health response
summary: Pungent odors wafting from the Chiquita Canyon Landfill prompted Los Angeles County officials to relocate residents after drilling unleashed a geyser of trash and fumes.
story: Pungent odors wafting from the Chiquita Canyon Landfill prompted Los Angeles County officials to order the company responsible to pay to relocate nearby residents after a drilling issue unleashed a geyser of trash and fumes.

Members of the fire department responded to the landfill Monday afternoon after a drill released gas into the air. The incident caused a plume of what appeared to be thick black smoke to rise, though it later turned white, according to NBC Los Angeles.
A “routine” operation was being done to install a new gas well to help with elevated temperatures, according to a statement Tuesday from Waste Connections, which owns and operates the site.
A pressurized pocket within the landfill was affected in the process, it said.
“This resulted in an above-ground release of gases and particulate material at the drilling location,” the company said. “No liquids were released, and no injuries have been reported.”
Drilling stopped and four people were taken to the hospital for evaluation, but Waste Connections said that no injuries have been reported.

The company is conducting air monitoring at the site as well as the local community. There were no indications that there was an excess of chemicals from based on California’s Reference Exposure Levels, the statement said.
“Chiquita continues to coordinate with state and local regulatory agencies and emergency response personnel,” Waste Connections said.

Los Angeles County’s public health department issued an emergency order Tuesday to have Waste Connections and Chiquita Canyon, LLC, provide immediate relief to the surrounding communities that are exposed to the “noxious odors.”

The order instructs the companies to provide residents with indoor spaces meant to provide relief from the odors, to provide short-term hotel stays for the immediate relocation of residents, and transportation for those who require assistance to reach those places.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
It also ordered that residents be provided support to improve their indoor air quality, such as air filters or purifiers.
Chiquita Canyon Landfill “has an obligation to timely and immediately provide relief to mitigate the exposures in the community,” the order said.

The work that was being done at the landfill was part of an Environmental Protection Agency order to properly handle the waste and mitigate odors at the landfill. The agency said that the landfill has seen a “significant subsurface elevated temperature event” since around May 2022.
The order included directives to redirect offgas by the end of this month.
Los Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger described the “explosion and methane plume” as “unacceptable” in a post on X Monday night.
“I will be demanding answers and accountability,” Barger wrote.

title: Apple reports outages after internal update, says it is working to get systems back online
summary: Apple said it was experiencing tech issues Tuesday that were affecting several of its popular consumer-facing services.
story: Apple said it was experiencing tech issues Tuesday that were affecting several of its popular consumer-facing services.
As of 2 p.m. ET, Apple’s own system status page showed that Apple Business, Apple School Manager, AppleCare, iCloud Mail and Web Apps, and SchoolWork were each experiencing outages.
Earlier, the page showed the App Store and Apple Music  experiencied outages.
For Subscribers

“Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning,” an Apple spokesperson told NBC News. “We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible.”

At Apple stores in New York and Chicago, employees told NBC News earlier in the day that their internal software had stopped working and they had been unable to complete purchases or make appointments.
For Subscribers
Over the past week, U.S. residents have experienced a cascade of technical issues that have led to nationwide outages of key consumer services, including email, air travel and online banking.

While none of the issues appear to be related, they’ve exposed America’s reliance on older infrastructure and revealed the extent to which companies and governments are being forced to upgrade systems in the AI age. The incidents have also stoked unfounded paranoia that something larger may be afoot.

title: Ray Tintori, filmmaker and boyfriend of ‘SNL’ alum Heidi Gardner, dies at 43
summary: Filmmaker Ray Tintori, the boyfriend of former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Heidi Gardner, has died, the New York City medical examiner’s office confirmed Tuesday.
story: Filmmaker Ray Tintori, the boyfriend of former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Heidi Gardner, has died, the New York City medical examiner’s office confirmed Tuesday.
Tintori was 43, and the agency did not provide the cause of death.
“We are investigating and the cause and manner of death are pending further study,” a spokesperson for the agency said in an email to NBC News.

Fire and EMS personnel responded to a request for a wellness check at a New York City apartment on Nov. 10, where one person was pronounced deceased upon arrival, a New York City Fire Department spokesperson said.
There was no immediate comment from Gardner, who left “SNL” in August 2025 after eight seasons with the show.
But pinned to the top of Tintori’s Instagram page was a July 27, 2025 post in which he wrote “Happy birthday to the angel of reality @heidilgardner.”
Gardner was born July 27, 1983.

“Prettier and more graceful than the moon and by far the coolest person I’ve ever met,” he wrote. “My favorite song in the world is you singing softly in my ear. My favorite color is the gold at the center of your eyes.”
Tintori also called her the “sexiest woman who ever lived.”
“The world is a love letter to you,” he wrote in closing. “I am your boy forever.”
The son of film editor John Tintori and the late script supervisor Mary Cybulski, Tintori is best known for the psychedelic music videos he directed for the indie bands MGMT and Arcade Fire.
In addition, Tintori directed videos for musical acts such as Chairlift, Bonnie Prince Billy, The Cool Kids, The Killers and Solange.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Tintori was also a founding member of Court 13, the filmmaking collective behind the movie “Beasts of the Southern Wild.” He was the special effects unit director on the 2012 film, which was nominated for four Oscars.
In 2017, Tintori won a Sports Emmy for co-directing “Follow My Lead: The Story of the 2016 NBA Finals,” a 360-degree virtual reality documentary.
Most recently, Tintori in 2025 co-directed a performance of Ethan Coen’s one-act play “Waiting.”
Tintori also had a cameo as a newsreel photographer in the 2025 movie “Marty Supreme.”

title: Classified NSA network went down, but no indication it was an attack, sources say
summary: A classified computer network used by the National Security Agency went down due to a technical problem Tuesday, but there was no indication that it was an attack, sources say
story: WASHINGTON — A classified computer network used by the National Security Agency went down due to a technical problem Tuesday, but there was no indication that it was caused by an attack, according to two people with knowledge of the matter and a senior U.S. cybersecurity official.

The NSA’s network issue came amid mass outages that have wreaked havoc on air travel, banks and emails over the past few days. Though such mass outages in quick succession are rare, U.S. officials say there is no sign that the technical problems were caused by a coordinated cyberattack.

President Donald Trump, when asked about the outages during his trip to the Philippines, said: “It’s life, it’s life. When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine.”

The NSA outage happened during maintenance on the network, the sources said. There was no sign that the outage affected the work of the NSA, which oversees America’s vast electronic surveillance efforts. It is not uncommon for government networks to suffer from brief disruptions or outages.
CNN first reported on the network going down.
A U.S. official said in a statement that “the National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The official added: “While some internal systems were affected, mission/critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend National Security continues.”

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton appeared on both CNBC and Fox Business Tuesday, where he stressed that from his view, the incidents seem to be the result of companies and organizations patching their systems to update or make them better.
“This is not a cyber attack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state. We’ve looked very closely,” he said.

Emily Harding, a former CIA analyst now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank, said that government systems “are highly redundant, so an outage like this won’t stop the work of national security.”
“Government systems generally are outdated and in need of repair. This is another wake-up call to invest in better systems,” she said.
The NSA incident came after a series of online outages and disruptions in recent days affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration’s systems, JPMorgan Chase and United Airlines.
The widely used online systems have long been a part of Americans’ daily lives. The outages have raised questions about technological vulnerabilities.
James Lewis, a former senior government official and cybersecurity expert, said it was “a little unusual” for the NSA to have this kind of problem. “But across the government, it’s fairly common.”

“It’s because the software is so complicated; it’s not always up to date,” he said. “When people try to patch it, they break it. So, it probably happens a lot more than we hear because it’s agencies that people don’t have as much interest in. But for NSA, it’s unusual. They probably weren’t affected by it, but it’s not that unusual to have systems crash.”
Tom Winter reported from New York. Dan De Luce, Gordon Lubold and Julie Tsirkin reported from Washington.

title: Jeffries endorses expansive health care agenda for Democratic Congress
summary: WASHINGTON — House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N
story: WASHINGTON — House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., is calling for an aggressive health care agenda next year for the new Democratic majorities in Congress.

Jeffries, who is the heavy favorite to become speaker of the House on Jan. 3, said Democrats should use their “historic” House majority and “robust” Senate majority to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage under the program to include benefits for dental, vision and hearing.
He also backed universal health coverage for children.

“We should lower the age of Medicare eligibility. We should expand coverage to include vision, hearing, and dental. And we should cover all the kids in the United States of America,” Jeffries said Tuesday in response to a question from NBC News. “Those are bold actions, meaningful actions, important actions that can be taken on our march toward universal health coverage.”

The remarks by Jeffries go significantly further than the pre-election health care agenda he laid out in September, which focused on undoing President Donald Trump’s Medicaid spending cuts and restoring enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits that expired in January.

The Democratic leader reiterated his call for those policies on Tuesday, in addition to funding medical research for pediatric cancer, among other areas. He said Congress must go further, though he didn’t say what age to set Medicare eligibility at.

“Right out of the gate, we will aggressively work on fixing the extraordinary damage that’s been done,” he said. “But we also know, as Democrats, that a return to the status quo is not acceptable. ... As part of our commitment that goes all the way back to FDR and Harry Truman to achieving universal access to health care for the American people.”

Jeffries kept the door open when asked if he favors advancing health care measures in a filibuster-proof “reconciliation” bill that can bypass the Senate’s 60-vote threshold and pass without any Republican support. That would make such a bill more likely to land on Trump’s desk, forcing him to decide whether to sign it into law.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Democrats are currently on pace to end up with 259 House seats and 56 Senate seats (with Alaska likely to be won by Democrats), according to NBC News estimates and projections.
“Given the majorities that we’ll have in the House and the Senate, our two respective caucuses are going to have to work their will in conversation with each other,” Jeffries said.

Among other key committee chairs who would be involved in negotiating such a bill, Jeffries mentioned “Bernie Sanders, the OG from Brooklyn,” who will chair the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee.

Sen. Sanders, I-Vt., the leading champion of Medicare for All, said that Jeffries appears to be “essentially supporting the first year” of his Medicare for All proposal, which he said includes a Medicare eligibility age of 55, plus extending benefits and covering all children.
“Medicare for All is a four-year transition program,” Sanders said, adding that the Jeffries’ approach would represent good progress.

title: Remains of woman who vanished in 2024 found in New Jersey Pine Barrens
summary: The remains of a 37-year-old woman who vanished more than two years ago in the New Jersey Pine Barrens were found Saturday during a multiagency search, state police said.
story: The remains of a 37-year-old woman who vanished more than two years ago in the New Jersey Pine Barrens were found Saturday during a multiagency search, state police said.

A search operation was being conducted within the Brendan T. Byrne State Forest in Burlington County in connection with the April 2024 disappearance of Danielle Lopez. A forensic examination identified the remains as belonging to Lopez, New Jersey State Police said in a news release Monday.
A cause and manner of death were not released, and police said the case remains active.

Lopez was last seen on April 13, 2024, by witnesses who saw her walking on Lost Lane, a dirt road in a heavily wooded area in Woodland Township, authorities previously told NBC’s “Dateline.” A detective said her car was found on the road in a large puddle of water. Some of Lopez’s personal belongings were in the car, but police found no signs of suspicious activity.
Authorities searched the area but did not find Lopez.

About a year and a half ago, James Ramsey, a New Jersey private investigator, began looking into Lopez’s case, according to NBC Philadelphia. Ramsey told the news outlet that he received information last week about where Lopez’s remains were possibly located.

Ramsey said police already had a large-scale search planned when he received that information. Her remains were found in a location that investigators had previously searched, Ramsey said. He told NBC Philadelphia that the area has rough terrain.
For Subscribers
“Anyone who knows what the Pine Barrens in Jersey, it’s a labyrinth,” he said. “It’s a needle in a haystack.”
For Subscribers
Ramsey did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday. State police said no additional information was currently available.
Lopez’s mother, Sue Quackenbush, remembered her daughter as someone who “loved people and was always thinking of someone else first.”

“If everyone would follow Danielle’s lead with a random act of kindness — allowing patience at a traffic light, or buying a stranger’s coffee — and do it thinking that is what Danielle would do, that would be appreciated,” she told NBC Philadelphia in a statement.

story: Hardcover books are great until you’re lugging three of them in a tote bag or squinting at a paperback under a dim lamp. An e-reader fits a whole library into something lighter than a single paperback, and it goes wherever you do: a morning commute, the beach, the couch, a crowded airplane cabin.

And even though you aren’t flipping actual pages, many e-readers do what they can to feel like a real book. Most e-readers use an e-ink screen, which mimics the look of ink on paper, says Nick Tanzi, assistant director of the South Huntington Public Library. It’s easier on the eyes than the LCD screen you find in tablets and uses far less battery, he adds. E-readers are also lighter than tablets, easier to carry than hardcovers and can hold thousands of ebooks. How to shop for an e-reader
When choosing the right e-reader for your needs, experts recommend keeping the following criteria in mind:

“The most important feature of an e-reader is its screen,” says Mantha. E-reader screens are measured diagonally in inches from the top corner to the opposite bottom corner, and a large screen with easy-to-read text is preferred. Keep in mind that especially big screens aren’t as portable and may drain the battery faster, according to experts.

Higher resolutions (measured in PPI, or pixels per inch) translate to crisper text, which is easier on the eyes, according to our experts. Lower resolutions, on the other hand, can result in a blurry reading experience, says Tanzi. All of the e-readers on our list have a PPI of 300 for black and white content.

Like most other devices, e-reader storage is measured in GB — the higher the number, the more books your device can store locally. Ebooks are generally small files, meaning that an e-reader can store hundreds, if not thousands of titles, says Tanzi. Keep in mind that picture books, graphic novels and other visual media take up substantially more storage space. For reference, 32GB of storage can hold up to 24,000 ebooks, according to Kobo.

Most e-readers last for weeks between charges. However, certain features like bright backlights and note-taking may drain the battery faster, and brands’ advertised battery life always varies depending on use.

Different e-reader manufacturers allow access to different e-book stores, and not all e-books are available on all storefronts. For example, Kindle allows users to purchase e-books through the Amazon store, while Kobo devices use the Kobo bookstore. Some devices let you transfer e-book files from your computer to your e-reader.
Kindle vs. Kindle Paperwhite
The Amazon Kindle and Amazon Kindle Paperwhite are two of the most popular e-readers you can buy. But it can be hard to tell them apart at a glance — they look almost identical in online photos.

The Amazon Kindle Paperwhite is essentially an upgraded Amazon Kindle. It’s a little larger, has a sleeker design, gets double the battery life (12 weeks), is IPX8 waterproof and has an adjustable color temperature. The regular Amazon Kindle, by contrast, is smaller, gets only six weeks of battery life, isn’t waterproof and lacks the ability to adjust the color temperature. It is much less expensive, however. Reading on both devices is similar, as they both run the same software and have the same Kindle bookstore.

If you can afford it, we highly recommend the Kindle Paperwhite over the regular Kindle. Being able to adjust the color temperature or warm light of the screen is a big deal: it makes reading in dark environments much easier on your eyes, in our experience. IPX8 waterproofing is also a huge peace of mind feature — you can read the Paperwhite by the pool, at the beach or in the bathtub without worry.
Frequently asked questions

A tablet is more like a phone or computer, meant to run hundreds of apps including productivity tools, video games and photo editing software. An e-reader is specifically designed and optimized for reading — it’s why the screens typically use e-ink and battery life is typically measured in weeks, not days.

You can use your public library card to borrow ebooks, audiobooks and other material for free, just as you would going to the library in person. Multiple NBC Selected staffers use the Libby app to connect to their public library account and borrow books for free. Most e-readers sync with the Libby app and will let you easily import borrowed ebooks to your device.

title: Gas geyser and noxious odor from L.A. area landfill prompts public health response
summary: Pungent odors wafting from the Chiquita Canyon Landfill prompted Los Angeles County officials to relocate residents after drilling unleashed a geyser of trash and fumes.
story: Pungent odors wafting from the Chiquita Canyon Landfill prompted Los Angeles County officials to order the company responsible to pay to relocate nearby residents after a drilling issue unleashed a geyser of trash and fumes.

Members of the fire department responded to the landfill Monday afternoon after a drill released gas into the air. The incident caused a plume of what appeared to be thick black smoke to rise, though it later turned white, according to NBC Los Angeles.
A “routine” operation was being done to install a new gas well to help with elevated temperatures, according to a statement Tuesday from Waste Connections, which owns and operates the site.
A pressurized pocket within the landfill was affected in the process, it said.
“This resulted in an above-ground release of gases and particulate material at the drilling location,” the company said. “No liquids were released, and no injuries have been reported.”
Drilling stopped and four people were taken to the hospital for evaluation, but Waste Connections said that no injuries have been reported.

The company is conducting air monitoring at the site as well as the local community. There were no indications that there was an excess of chemicals from based on California’s Reference Exposure Levels, the statement said.
“Chiquita continues to coordinate with state and local regulatory agencies and emergency response personnel,” Waste Connections said.

Los Angeles County’s public health department issued an emergency order Tuesday to have Waste Connections and Chiquita Canyon, LLC, provide immediate relief to the surrounding communities that are exposed to the “noxious odors.”

The order instructs the companies to provide residents with indoor spaces meant to provide relief from the odors, to provide short-term hotel stays for the immediate relocation of residents, and transportation for those who require assistance to reach those places.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
It also ordered that residents be provided support to improve their indoor air quality, such as air filters or purifiers.
Chiquita Canyon Landfill “has an obligation to timely and immediately provide relief to mitigate the exposures in the community,” the order said.

The work that was being done at the landfill was part of an Environmental Protection Agency order to properly handle the waste and mitigate odors at the landfill. The agency said that the landfill has seen a “significant subsurface elevated temperature event” since around May 2022.
The order included directives to redirect offgas by the end of this month.
Los Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger described the “explosion and methane plume” as “unacceptable” in a post on X Monday night.
“I will be demanding answers and accountability,” Barger wrote.

title: 8-year-old Haitian boy returns home after being detained by ICE in San Diego
summary: The 8-year-old Haitian boy who ICE detained in San Diego nearly two weeks ago has been reunited with his family, advocates with Haitian Bridge Alliance said on Monday.
story: The 8-year-old Haitian boy who ICE detained in San Diego nearly two weeks ago has been reunited with his family, advocates with Haitian Bridge Alliance said on Monday.

The boy, a third grader at Fay Elementary School in City Heights, was taken into federal custody on Nov. 4. Video recorded by volunteer observer Karen Pohl at the federal building shows three armed federal agents walking the boy away from ICE’s field office and into an elevator.

That video spread, sparking outrage and protest, and reaching national coverage. Last Thursday, protesters, many of them carrying signs, called for the released of the boy outside the Edward J. Schwartz federal building in downtown San Diego, where ICE holds its offices.

Now, new signs saying “welcome home” decorate the office of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, which worked to bring him back to his family. The organization, the boy and his family all said they are happy to be back together after a difficult wait.
While in federal custody, the boy was taken to a facility in Texas, the organization said.

“The aunt was literally crying, and she said, ‘I have not eaten since the Wednesday they took my baby.’ They haven’t been able to sleep because of that,” said Guerline Jozef, of the Haitian Bridge Alliance. “The cousins were there when they took him, and wondering: will they ever see him again? But today [Monday] they are able to see him again. They are able to hug him. They are able to, you know, rub his head and show how much they missed and love him,” Jozef said.
For Subscribers

The boy previously had Temporary Protected Status and was living with his uncle after his father was deported last year. ICE called the family for a check-in and said the uncle couldn’t establish legal guardianship, so they took the child into custody for his safety, the agency said.
For Subscribers
Congressman Juan Vargas represents the family and intervened with the federal government to secure the boy’s release.

“The people that I was able to talk to, some that I knew pretty well, I said, ‘Well, what are you guys doing?’ And they were saying, ‘Well, you know, they just look at numbers and that’s what they’re looking at right now. They’re trying to get numbers,” Vargas said.
The boy told NBC 7 he loves Haitian food and he hoped to have that for dinner Monday night. He said he’s looking forward to returning to school, where his favorite class is P.E., this week.

title: Remains of woman who vanished in 2024 found in New Jersey Pine Barrens
summary: The remains of a 37-year-old woman who vanished more than two years ago in the New Jersey Pine Barrens were found Saturday during a multiagency search, state police said.
story: The remains of a 37-year-old woman who vanished more than two years ago in the New Jersey Pine Barrens were found Saturday during a multiagency search, state police said.

A search operation was being conducted within the Brendan T. Byrne State Forest in Burlington County in connection with the April 2024 disappearance of Danielle Lopez. A forensic examination identified the remains as belonging to Lopez, New Jersey State Police said in a news release Monday.
A cause and manner of death were not released, and police said the case remains active.

Lopez was last seen on April 13, 2024, by witnesses who saw her walking on Lost Lane, a dirt road in a heavily wooded area in Woodland Township, authorities previously told NBC’s “Dateline.” A detective said her car was found on the road in a large puddle of water. Some of Lopez’s personal belongings were in the car, but police found no signs of suspicious activity.
Authorities searched the area but did not find Lopez.

About a year and a half ago, James Ramsey, a New Jersey private investigator, began looking into Lopez’s case, according to NBC Philadelphia. Ramsey told the news outlet that he received information last week about where Lopez’s remains were possibly located.

Ramsey said police already had a large-scale search planned when he received that information. Her remains were found in a location that investigators had previously searched, Ramsey said. He told NBC Philadelphia that the area has rough terrain.
For Subscribers
“Anyone who knows what the Pine Barrens in Jersey, it’s a labyrinth,” he said. “It’s a needle in a haystack.”
For Subscribers
Ramsey did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday. State police said no additional information was currently available.
Lopez’s mother, Sue Quackenbush, remembered her daughter as someone who “loved people and was always thinking of someone else first.”

“If everyone would follow Danielle’s lead with a random act of kindness — allowing patience at a traffic light, or buying a stranger’s coffee — and do it thinking that is what Danielle would do, that would be appreciated,” she told NBC Philadelphia in a statement.

title: Ray Tintori, filmmaker and boyfriend of ‘SNL’ alum Heidi Gardner, dies at 43
summary: Filmmaker Ray Tintori, the boyfriend of former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Heidi Gardner, has died, the New York City medical examiner’s office confirmed Tuesday.
story: Filmmaker Ray Tintori, the boyfriend of former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Heidi Gardner, has died, the New York City medical examiner’s office confirmed Tuesday.
Tintori was 43, and the agency did not provide the cause of death.
“We are investigating and the cause and manner of death are pending further study,” a spokesperson for the agency said in an email to NBC News.

Fire and EMS personnel responded to a request for a wellness check at a New York City apartment on Nov. 10, where one person was pronounced deceased upon arrival, a New York City Fire Department spokesperson said.
There was no immediate comment from Gardner, who left “SNL” in August 2025 after eight seasons with the show.
But pinned to the top of Tintori’s Instagram page was a July 27, 2025 post in which he wrote “Happy birthday to the angel of reality @heidilgardner.”
Gardner was born July 27, 1983.

“Prettier and more graceful than the moon and by far the coolest person I’ve ever met,” he wrote. “My favorite song in the world is you singing softly in my ear. My favorite color is the gold at the center of your eyes.”
Tintori also called her the “sexiest woman who ever lived.”
“The world is a love letter to you,” he wrote in closing. “I am your boy forever.”
The son of film editor John Tintori and the late script supervisor Mary Cybulski, Tintori is best known for the psychedelic music videos he directed for the indie bands MGMT and Arcade Fire.
In addition, Tintori directed videos for musical acts such as Chairlift, Bonnie Prince Billy, The Cool Kids, The Killers and Solange.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Tintori was also a founding member of Court 13, the filmmaking collective behind the movie “Beasts of the Southern Wild.” He was the special effects unit director on the 2012 film, which was nominated for four Oscars.
In 2017, Tintori won a Sports Emmy for co-directing “Follow My Lead: The Story of the 2016 NBA Finals,” a 360-degree virtual reality documentary.
Most recently, Tintori in 2025 co-directed a performance of Ethan Coen’s one-act play “Waiting.”
Tintori also had a cameo as a newsreel photographer in the 2025 movie “Marty Supreme.”

title: I Study James Bond for a Living. Here’s How I Reacted to the Robert Pattinson Casting (and Who I Would’ve Picked)
summary: What do James Bond experts think of Robert Pattinson’s casting?
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this, James Bond scholars weigh in on Robert Pattinson’s casting.
James Bond fans who waited seven long years to find out which actor would be the next to play the iconic British spy have gotten their answer.
Pattison, Robert Pattinson.
Amazon MGM, which owns the rights to the Bond films, announced the choice on Nov. 16, which predictably left longtime fans either shaken or stirred.

That also goes for a trio of Bond scholars who spoke about the choice of the 40-year-old star of “The Batman” and “The Odyssey” to succeed Daniel Craig, whose last Bond film was released in 2021. If the next Bond film is not released until 2028, it will have been the longest hiatus between movies in the franchise’s 64-year history, so the fans are thirsty for a new version.
TODAY.com discussed the casting choice with:

Oliver Buckton, the author of the Ian Fleming biography “The World Is Not Enough” and a professor and chair of the Department of English at Florida Atlantic UniversityColin Burnett, program director of Film & Media Studies at Washington University in St. Louis, and author of the forthcoming book, “James Bond and the Art of Franchise Storytelling”James Chapman, the author of “Licence to Thrill: A Cultural History of the James Bond Films.”
Oliver Buckton, the author of the Ian Fleming biography “The World Is Not Enough” and a professor and chair of the Department of English at Florida Atlantic University
Colin Burnett, program director of Film & Media Studies at Washington University in St. Louis, and author of the forthcoming book, “James Bond and the Art of Franchise Storytelling”
James Chapman, the author of “Licence to Thrill: A Cultural History of the James Bond Films.”
Here’s what they had to say.
A ‘Surprise’ Casting
Pattinson came on late as a candidate after it was previously reported that actors Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult had all undergone screen tests for the role in October.

“I was surprised, to be honest,” Buckton tells TODAY.com. “I think like a lot of people, we had in mind a shortlist that didn’t include him. But having time to think about it, it does make sense in a number of ways.”
“My immediate reaction was, ‘Wow, I wasn’t really expecting that,’ and then I got really excited about the idea,” Chapman says.
“At no point in history has a major A-list star been cast as James Bond at the peak of their career.”
Colin Burnett said on what makes Pattinson's casting remarkable
Burnett called Pattinson’s casting “a tectonic shift” in the way the role has been filled in the past.

“At no point in history has a major A-list star been cast as James Bond at the peak of their career,” Burnett says. “They have had reasonable careers, but Pattinson is someone who comes in aware of his stardom, of his box office potential, of his performance, and who’s very much going to look forward to steering the franchise. None of the previous actors had the clout on the way in to do that.”
Why Robert Pattinson’s Casting Makes Sense
The recurring theme that came up as to why Pattinson got the nod is simple: box office dollars.

Amazon MGM Studios took creative control of the Bond franchise in 2025 after making a deal with the franchise’s longtime producers, Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The change came four years after Amazon bought MGM, which owned the rights to the James Bond films, for $8.5 billion.

The online retail giant did not pay all that money to have the next Bond film to flop at the box office. That made going the traditional Bond route of casting an up-and-coming actor who is not yet widely known to the public, like Craig and former Bond actors Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan, a gamble.

“I think that there’s so much at stake in this casting decision now with Amazon taking over and relaunching the whole franchise in a different way that they didn’t want to take a risk on an actor who hasn’t been in major films,” Buckton says.

“I know for a fact, having spoken to people inside Amazon, that they are hoping for and building the structure of Amazon MGM off a massive box office success (with Bond),” Burnett says. “What they’re hoping is to have a big hit right from the get-go, so that too is a major shift.”
Does Robert Pattinson Look the Part?

At 40, Pattinson is about the right age to play the superspy, who is generally considered to be in his late 30s, 40-ish in the Ian Fleming novels that made the character famous. The oldest actor to be cast as Bond was Roger Moore, who was 45 at the time.

Pattinson is also tall, lithe and dark-haired, which is closer to Fleming’s description of the character than Craig, who initially dealt with a wave of backlash about being blonde, short and muscular when he was first cast.
“People will feel just because of Pattinson’s look in a tuxedo with his hair back that he is James Bond, much more so than Daniel Craig,” Burnett says.
In an eerie coincidence, Pattinson resembles a cartoon rendering of Bond that Fleming had made in the late 1950s when he had a comic strip done of the character, according to Buckton.
“Fleming’s model was the 1930s star Hoagy Carmichael, but it looks uncannily like Robert Pattinson,” Buckton says.
Is Robert Pattinson Too Famous to Play Bond?
Will fans see James Bond on the screen or Robert Pattinson?

That is a question that has not been a problem for the six previous Bond actors, including the legendary Sean Connery, because they were not household names when they landed the role. The role made them famous.

“That’s the risk they’re taking, that he has too much baggage from other films,” Buckton says. “But he’s such a chameleon. Look at all the different roles he’s played, from ‘Twilight’ to ‘The Batman’ to movies like ‘The Lighthouse.’ I think they’re counting on him being able to do that again and reinvent himself as James Bond, and the fans will accept that.”
“The thing with Robert Pattinson is he changes with the times,” Burnett says. “He’s constantly reinventing himself.”

His experience in carrying big-budget films could actually be an asset rather than a drawback, according to the experts. It helps that he has already worked with director Denis Villeneuve on the “Dune” films because Villeneuve has committed to directing the next Bond film.

“He’s got that kind of crossover aspect to him,” Chapman says. “He’s done big franchise properties, big successful films with a female fanbase, so there’s real acting credentials there. He’s not a one-note actor. I’m thinking he can play Bond in a different way than he plays Batman.”
However, there’s also the possibility of overexposure if he’s also appearing in “Batman” and “Dune” movies in the midst of “Bond” films.

“Some of the negative reaction has been, let’s not have one actor taking on these iconic roles at the same time,” Buckton says. “That’s the risk, that Bond fans are like, ‘We want our own guy.  We want someone who’s not already Superman or Batman or whatever.’”
What Robert Pattinson Could Bring to the Role
Each of the previous six actors brought their own touch to the role, from the suave and sly Sean Connery to the campy Roger Moore to the brooding Daniel Craig.
Pattinson leaned in to a dark portrayal of Batman, so it remains to be seen how he balances the humor, physical prowess and romantic banter with the Bond girls in the new film.

“(Craig) became this wounded, dark, introspective James Bond, and I thought the new Bond would have to be a bit lighter,” Buckton says. “Even though (Pattinson) has played some dark characters, I think he has enough versatility. I would expect a little bit of a throwback to more of a suave, calm-under-pressure James Bond, and maybe a bit more of the Bond girl chemistry, which wasn’t Daniel Craig’s strong suit.”
“If Pattinson had come around and there had been no Craig, it would have been no problem to play more of a dark, psychological version, but Craig has cleared this ground already,” Burnett says.
Buckton speculated that maybe Pattinson’s performance in the Christopher Nolan movie “Tenet” could be a hint at what he does with Bond.
“I think that’s a glimpse of what he might be like because there’s something kind of edgy about him that I like, and maybe that’s what made him the choice,” he said.
Who Would Bond Experts Have Chosen?
Buckton liked “Superman” star Henry Cavill, 43, who was in the running for the role in the early 2000s as a 22-year-old but lost out to Craig.
Buckton would’ve gone with Callum Turner this time around.

“I could see him as Bond,” he says of Turner. “Some people say he didn’t have the charisma, but that’s something you can grow into. He could be identified as James Bond because he’s not a huge star right now, and I think he could bring that humor and a lighter touch to the role.”
Burnett would’ve gone with “Frankenstein” and “Wuthering Heights” star Jacob Elordi.

“I saw ‘Wuthering Heights’ in the theater and there’s a scene where he reemerges onscreen and the theater just swooned,” Burnett says. “That’s a star. That’s a thing Bond has always had. Men want to be like him and women want to be with him. Elordi has that feel.”

title: Jennifer Lopez Says She’s the ‘Happiest I’ve Been’ and Credits This 1 Change in Her Love Life
summary: Jennifer Lopez says she’s single, opens up about her divorces and the ‘JLo Show’ in new interview with Hoda Kotb on the TODAY show and podcast ‘Making Space.’
story: After decades in the public eye and four divorces, Jennifer Lopez is no stranger to love, both feeling and talking about it. The complex emotion was a major theme in her lengthy sit-down with friend and former TODAY anchor Hoda Kotb, which aired in part on TODAY Nov. 17. The full extended version will be available as an episode of  the “Making Space” podcast Nov. 18.

“The thing for me is to be the love in the room,” Lopez, 57, told Hoda, 62. “To put love out into the world. To remind people that love exists. ... Love yourself and remember who you are. I’ve been on that journey, and once you remember who you are, you wanna remind others. ... I feel like for me, since (I was) very young, without knowing it, that’s been my purpose.”

Hoda then revealed that one of the qualities she admires most about Lopez is her ability to fall in love. That prompted Hoda to share that she’s not sure if she’s ever been in love herself — “which gives me chills, and also makes me a little sad because it takes guts,” Hoda added.
“It takes a fearlessness,” Lopez responded before explaining why she’s fine without having romantic love at the moment.

“What you realize is what you’re searching for in another person is only up to you,” Lopez explained. “I have the ability to fall in love every day with my life, with the cup of coffee, with the bath, with the song I created that day.”
“The only way you really learn these lessons is to make mistakes, to fail, to have things not work out the way you thought they were.”
“It’s been kind of a two or three-year journey for me of really trying to understand myself, what my purpose is and what love is. And that for me has been a joy.”
She said she’s since realized that love isn’t what makes you happy, but rather that you should make yourself happy.

“You have to really understand that that is in your hands, and it’s how you wake up every day. ... It’s how you choose to walk through the world, understanding your power, understanding everything about yourself that is only you uniquely and what you have to offer to the world. And I think for me, that made me look at romantic relationships differently, as well, because it’s not something that I need. It’s something that I would like.”
“I have been the happiest I’ve been the past few years, where I’ve been single,” Lopez laughed. “But it took time to get there for me because I was such and I still am very much romantic.”
Lopez is now able to see the positive in this mindset though, she told Hoda.

“I used to beat that part of myself up. Like, that’s the reason I made these choices and these mistakes, and I’ve had these failures. ... I’ve been divorced several times. My kids didn’t have the things that I wanted them to have.”
“And then you realize ... that romantic is the person who is able to go out into the world and create a life that I could have never dreamed of when I was growing up in the Bronx.”

She said she sometimes struggled with how much of her personal life she made public. “I felt like it really overshadowed some of the work that I did and the things that I was really proud of ... And hurt me with opportunities as well, I think.”

“Your star celebrity part of you becomes bigger than the work that you’re doing. And I would look at other people’s careers and go, ‘Why don’t they get this type of scrutiny? Why is it me?’” she chuckled.

“I have to take responsibility in that I was very open about my life. I’ve never been kind of a guarded person in that way. I always wore my heart on my sleeve and was a very open book. And what I realize is that you have to have boundaries. That’s part of loving yourself. That’s part of it.”

A recent, major change in Lopez’s life that’s allowed her more time to reflect is becoming an empty nester. Her twins, whom she shares with ex-husband Marc Anthony, recently left for college. But, like any other parent, she helped them decorate their rooms, sobbed and went on her way.

“It was the first time I’ve lived alone in I don’t know how long, so that was really weird,” Lopez recalled. “Not having them down the hall does something to your heart. But I also realized I do enjoy my own company.”

“I enjoy my space, and I never was like that. I was always so afraid of the quiet and of being alone. I think that’s what drove me to make some decisions that weren’t the best for me in my life. But I really feel at peace there in my house that I’ve built.”
This major lifestyle change has helped inspire her in the recording studio, as well.

“I’ve made some songs that really feel very me right now. They’re a little bit unapologetic. They’re very different than things that I’ve dared to write before,” Lopez said. “A lot of 20-year-olds ... make the pop music. I made the pop music when I was in my 20s, and I write for me and for people who experience what I’m experiencing. And it’s a different type of feeling. I think it’s important to do that, to have that voice out there, too.”

The rom-com star is also focused on another creative project: the Thanksgiving Day release of her concert film, “The JLo Show: Live From Las Vegas.” The title is a play on how public her life has been over the past few decades.

“Yes, you’re watching ‘The JLo Show,’ me singing and dancing. But also, I started out watching ‘West Side Story’ on Thanksgiving in front of that TV, thinking about being an entertainer. I never thought that also my life, my personal life, would become the show and everything about me would be fair game,” Lopez explained.

“I didn’t think about the fame side of this. I just thought, ‘I wanna sing and dance and act. That’s what I wanna do with my life.’ This other part that comes along with it. And so, it’s a real, interwoven piece about a mini-musical of my life.”
So what’s next for the icon in her personal life? She told Hoda she’s setting boundaries and open to romantic partnership if it comes her way — but not just with anyone.

“You get to a point where you have a certain standard, because if I’m on the floor or if I’m up here, it doesn’t matter,” Lopez said. “Is there somebody who can match who you are and the love that you’re capable of giving?”
“Life is gonna take you in all those different directions, but having somebody who sees you and loves you in all of those iterations is really the goal.”

The full “Making Space” episode with Jennifer Lopez comes out November 18th. Watch it on YouTube or listen on Spotify. Check out Season 9 of “Making Space” for conversations with Ina Garten, Mariska Hargitay, Sandra Bullock and more!

title: A Complicated Friendship Inspired Lucy Tan’s ‘Tiger’s Mouth,’ the Latest Book From Jenna Bush Hager’s Imprint
summary: “Tiger’s Mouth,” the latest book out from Jenna Bush Hager’s Thousand Voices x Random House Publishing Group, is the story of a charged friendship.
story: “Tiger’s Mouth,” the latest book out from Jenna Bush Hager’s Thousand Voices x Random House Publishing Group, is the story of a charged friendship.
Jack Chen and Jack Owens meet at an internship and nearly immediately recognize each wants what the other has.

“In every relationship, whether it’s romantic or platonic, or professional, there’s a power balance. You hope it’s somewhat equal but often it’s not, and if it’s not, what then?” author Lucy Tan tells TODAY.com.

Tan’s first novel, “What We Were Promised,” was a family epic set in Shanghai. Her sophomore novel opens on the two Jacks crossing path one summer during a New York internship. Jack Owens may be the son of the company’s billionaire founder, but he lacks his father’s ambition, and also struggles with depression.

Jack Chen, on the other hand, comes from a family of caterers. Growing up, he studied rich kids and learned to act more like them to build a life like theirs. When he finesses his way into a prestigious internship meant for Columbia graduate students, Chen is ready to fake his way through everything.
“The characters we meet have entirely different lives but they both make each other feel seen,” Jenna says.
Tan, a Seattle bookseller, was inspired by a past personal friendship that had a complicated power dynamic. The questions that it raised drew her to write about privilege and interpersonal dynamics.

These tensions play out in the the two Jacks’ friendship. Chen longs for access to the resources and opportunities that Owens had growing up, while Owens longs for the love and care that Chen experienced.
Betrayal ends up driving the men apart, but their careers keep them in the same circle, where they compete like opponents in their favorite board game, Go.
Tan brings these men on a journey through platonic love and resentment, traversing the finite and abstract aspects of the world.
“Together they will decide: What is a life worth? And are some worth more than others?” Tan says.

title: McDonald’s Launches ‘Home Alone’ Meal Inspired by Kevin’s Cravings
summary: McDonald’s is lauching a “Home Alone” Meal, with a special McFlurry, fries and dipping sauce, 36 years after the Macaulay Culkin film premiered.
story: This yuletide season, McDonald’s is offering the gift of nostalgia.

Thirty-six years after the debut of the classic holiday movie, the burger behemoth announced the “Home Alone” Meal, with limited-time menu items and collectible socks, as well as in-person and virtual experiences. The Disney partnership meal will be available at participating restaurants nationwide starting Dec. 1, while supplies last.
McDonald’s has turned some of Kevin McCallister’s (Macaulay Culkin) most memorable movie moments into a trio of menu items, encased in a box designed to look like his family’s home:

Medium Little Nero’s Pizza McShaker Fries are inspired by the rambunctious kid’s go-to pizza (plain cheese), with McShaker seasoning (notes of tomato, garlic, Italian herbs and cheese) that you can add with a McShaker bag.

Medium Little Nero’s Pizza McShaker Fries are inspired by the rambunctious kid’s go-to pizza (plain cheese), with McShaker seasoning (notes of tomato, garlic, Italian herbs and cheese) that you can add with a McShaker bag.

Lovely Cheese Pizza Dipping Sauce, also inspired by McCallister’s preferred pizza, combines tomato flavor, Parmesan cheese, garden herbs and a hint of garlic. You get this sauce with the choice of Chicken McNuggets or McCrispy Strips, or you can just order it a la carte.

Lovely Cheese Pizza Dipping Sauce, also inspired by McCallister’s preferred pizza, combines tomato flavor, Parmesan cheese, garden herbs and a hint of garlic. You get this sauce with the choice of Chicken McNuggets or McCrispy Strips, or you can just order it a la carte.
Everything Sundae McFlurry features vanilla soft-serve swirled with hot fudge, Oreo cookie pieces and M&M’s, channeling Kevin’s room-service feast in “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York.”
Everything Sundae McFlurry features vanilla soft-serve swirled with hot fudge, Oreo cookie pieces and M&M’s, channeling Kevin’s room-service feast in “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York.”

Customers can collect one of four sock designs with their meal, including one inspired by the film’s most culturally enduring moment: Kevin’s scream. The other three socks feature Grimace, Birdy and the Hamburglar, who might’ve joined the Wet Bandits if they only stole Big Macs.
“Home Alone” came out 36 years ago, on Nov. 10, 1990. Culkin, who may have a reboot in the works, is starring an ad campaign for the partnership in which he enjoys time alone in an empty McDonald’s.

“What I love about this collaboration is that the Home Alone Meal captures something bigger than just one character, it’s about the playful spirit that resonates with people across generations,”  Culkin said in a press release. “Bringing this to life with McDonald’s and getting to reexperience these moments with my own kids, reminds me why fans keep coming back to Kevin’s story. That’s the magic we’re celebrating here.”

On Dec. 4 through Dec. 5 from 5 — 10 p.m. PT, the McDonald’s Home Alone Challenge, an immersive pop-up experience in Los Angeles, California, will let fans complete a series of challenges in themed, interactive rooms, like sliding into a ball pit or testing out your slingshot skills, for a free “Home Alone” Meal.
You can register for the experience here.

In the McDonald’s app, customers can redeem $5 off a $20 McDelivery order or use MyMcDonald’s Rewards points to redeem a 14-day free trial of the Disney+Hulu bundle, where they can access the “Home Alone” collection.
Customers also have the ability to round up their order cost to help Ronald McDonald House families stay together during a child’s medical journey.
Last year, McDonald’s partnered with another iconic Christmas movie, “The Grinch,” to launch a meal featuring Dill Pickle “Grinch Salt” McShaker Fries.

title: 25 Years Later, Watch Daniel Radcliffe Talk to TODAY in 2001 About Landing Harry Potter Role
summary: Daniel Radcliffe spoke with TODAY in 2001 before “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone” was released on Nov. 16.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment features an interview with Daniel Radcliffe on Nov. 12, 2001, shortly before the “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone,” the first film in the “Harry Potter” series, was released.

“Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone” brought the adventures of the young wizard from the page to the big screen. The film — the first of eight to be adapted from J.K. Rowling’s series of beloved books — opened Nov. 16, 2001.

On Nov. 12 of that year, newcomer Daniel Radcliffe, who landed the title role, sat down with TODAY’s Katie Couric to talk about the highly anticipated movie. This was the first of many appearances from the franchise’s stars on TODAY.
Radcliffe, who was 12 at the time of the interview, had recently attended the New York and London premieres of the film.
“It was pretty scary, but it was really good fun,” Radcliffe said. “And everybody there, like (director) Chris Columbus, he was there, and he just makes you feel really at ease.”
Were the premieres exciting after all the hard work that went into making the movie?
“It was fun, but I was quite nervous. But it was very cool,” he said.
How Did Daniel Radcliffe Land the Role of Harry Potter?

Radcliffe beat out thousands of hopefuls to snag the plum role — a part that would eventually set him up for a thriving career in Hollywood. He didn’t have any keen insight into just why he got the coveted lead role.
“I have no idea,” he told Couric.
“I really don’t know why they chose me, but I’m glad they did,” he continued.
How Did Daniel Radcliffe’s Parents Guide Him?

Radcliffe’s parents were somewhat worried when he was up for the part. He was not a household name yet at the point — his credits prior to the “Harry Potter” franchise included the British miniseries “David Copperfield” and the Pierce Brosnan movie “The Tailor of Panama.”
His parents knew it was no slam dunk he’d get the role.

“They only had one concern, and that was because I’ve been up for ‘David Copperfield’ and I’ve been up for ‘Tailor of Panama,’ and on both of those, I kind of had a tendency to get my hopes up,” he said. “And they knew that there were thousands of boys going up for the part, so they didn’t want me to get my hopes up and then be disappointed.”
Adding, “So they were just protecting me.”
Did Daniel Radcliffe Read the ‘Harry Potter’ Books?
Radcliffe didn’t read the books until after he was cast, but he was quickly enchanted by the world of Hogwarts. At the time, only four books in the seven-book series had been published.
However, after diving into the world, the actor said he was one of many people who could see themselves in Harry.

“It was the fact that, I think not only myself, but I think everybody can relate to Harry in some way ... it’s the idea of magic,” he said. “When magic kind of comes to life, there’s so much opportunity for absolutely anything to happen ... I kind of like to read about what would happen if magic really came to life.”

title: Beanie Feldstein Says Ariana Grande Saved Ben Stiller’s Life on Set of ‘Focker-In-Law’
summary: Beanie Feldstein reveals behind-the-scenes moments during the filming of “Focker-In-Law,” including how Ariana Grande saved Ben Stiller’s life.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Commercial Break,” TODAY.com catches up with guests between takes in Studio 1A for unfiltered moments and more questions.
Beanie Feldstein walks into the TODAY Lounge and instantly lights up the room with her smile and infectious personality.

The star of stage and hit films, including “Ladybird” and “Booksmart,” is visiting Studio 1A to talk about her latest project, “Focker-In-Law.” The fourth installment in the the “Meet the Parents” franchise, “Focker-In-Law” picks up 16 years after the last sequel (“Little Fockers”) left off, with Greg Focker’s (Ben Stiller) young twins all grown up and in relationships of their own.
Feldstein plays Stiller’s daughter, Samantha, and Skyler Gisondo is Henry, Stiller’s over-parented son who’s planning to propose to his girlfriend, Olivia (Ariana Grande).

The new movie, which hits theaters Nov. 25, reunites the original cast including Stiller, Robert De Niro, Blythe Danner, Teri Polo, Owen Wilson and Mr. Jinx (well, sort of), along with adding Feldstein, Gisondo, Grande and Eduardo Franco to the mix.

As expected, there are high jinks, mishaps, injuries and a whole lot of uncomfortable moments that make for pure comedy gold. Among them is Stiller doing a vocal performance that’s guaranteed to live on in YouTube infamy and a dinner table choking scene that became all too real, as Feldstein reveals when we sit down to talk.

Read on to find out how Grande stepped in to assist, how Feldstein felt about the Grammy-winner’s singing on set, as well as what it was like reuniting with her “Booksmart” co-stars and how they “got deep” during the filming of “Focker-In-Law.”
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.
I truly think it was like one of the most singularly joyful experiences I’ve ever had working on anything.

I think because Samantha’s so along for the ride and it was so fun to be like, “This is the support system,” but also the one calling everything out a little bit. I think because (Samantha) is so close to her dad, she’s able to like call him out in a way that feels like deeply loving and not mean.
And I got to be Ben Stiller’s daughter. Like, it was unbelievable.

John Hamburg, who’s our writer director, he co-wrote the first movie when he was 29. So, he’s grown up with these movies, working on them. And he said that Greg Focker is like a little bit of his own persona coming out.
He’s much less insane than Greg Focker, but he is a hovercraft dad in like the sweetest way.

I think that both Eduardo and I in real life, but also as Samantha and the character Eduardo — which obviously was written for him — we’re very earnest people, both of us. And I think we bring an earnestness to Samantha and Eduardo.
Even though they’re a little bit more artsy and a little bit less straitlaced than Henry (Gisondo), I think we bring like a little bit of the heartbeat, like the grounding force.

And Eduardo, the character, and Eduardo the person, are just so pure. He’s one of the most pure people I’ve ever known. And I think he brings this like genuineness and purity to the character, which is so unexpected and so fun.

Ari just sings all the time, like under her breath, when she’s like walking between sets and stuff. And obviously everyone’s like stopping and listening because it’s the Ariana Grande just like, you know, bebopping around.

We talked a lot of musical theater, but I don’t think we officially sang anything together. But Ari’s kind of just vocalizing all the time and everyone’s just like staring because it’s the most beautiful sound you’ve ever heard.
That moment was 100, and we filmed that for two full days. When I tell you, every single take, I laughed. Like there was not one time where I didn’t find it out-loud funny, even on the 60th take.

That was definitely the moment where it was this out-of-body experience of like, “I’m in ‘Meet the Parents’ and I’m watching ‘Meet the Parents.’ Like what is happening right now? This is one of the best days of my life.”
But those dinner table scenes I think are also so fun because we’re all together. The first one with Blythe (Danner) and it’s this real family togetherness. But, also, they’re so uncomfortable.

The other moment that was crazy was, I swear to God, I think Ben actually turned purple. Like he wasn’t acting. He was so committed to the choking on the steak that he literally turned purple and Ariana Grande saved his life. I swear to God.
He was so purple. He was like, “I was seeing stars. I couldn’t see for a second.” I was like, “Ben, you’ve taken it too far.”
Heaven. I love those boys. I would do anything for those boys.
Skyler and I have been joking, because we play lovers in “Booksmart,” and then he’s my brother (in “Focker-In-Law”). Now I need to play his mother next, in a flashback or something.
But, yeah, Skyler and I got to do a lot on “Booksmart,” so I feel like I came in like really knowing what to expect.

Eduardo and I don’t have as much to do together in “Booksmart,” we have like that big opening scene in the bathroom, but otherwise we’re kind of in separate worlds, which is kind of the setup of the movie.
So it was just heaven to get to be like literally right next to him for three months filming this movie. We had so much fun together.
I feel like we went so deep. We would ride together to work every day and we just got so deep, like deep heart-to-hearts.
And, yeah, “Samuardo Forever.” That was our little couple name. Samurado Forever. I think they’re a really funny, unexpected couple and it really works.

title: When J. Lo Joked About Her 4 Divorces, a Fan’s Witty Response Left Her Cackling: ‘Funniest Thing I Ever Heard’
summary: Jennifer Lopez laughed when a fan made a joke about her four divorces. Hear the line that cracked her up.
story: When it comes to the highs and lows of her very public love life, Jennifer Lopez has a sense of humor.
Over the weekend, the  “Ain’t It Funny” singer spoke to fans at a screening of her new TV special, “The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas,” at the 92nd Street Y in New York.
She said her four divorces are a “big part of my story.” The singer then said, “Four times,” and held up four fingers.
When a fan in the audience shouted, “You have six more fingers!” Lopez couldn’t help but laugh, per a video captured at the event.
“Yes I do!” she said as she excitedly tapped her feet on the floor and pointed into the crowd.
Lopez was clearly impressed with the witty comment and said, “Oh my God, that is the funniest thing I’ve ever heard in my life.”
Someone on the stage also acknowledged that the clever phrase has potential.
“That’s a T-shirt,” they said, prompting Lopez to agree.
In a video clip of the moment, the crowd erupted in laughter over the comedic exchange. Social media users also got a good giggle.
“You know its funny when you laugh and stomp at the same time,” one commented.
“Collect those rings,” another wrote.
One Instagram user said, “I’d buy that tshirt too!!!” and another embraced Lopez’s honesty, writing, “Right! Live your life.”
Marina Prut, the content creator who captured the video, called Lopez an “inspiration.”
“If she can work this hard, reaching new heights, fall and rise again — so can we,” she tells TODAY.com.

Lopez has been married four times. First to Ojani Noa for a year from 1997 to 1998, then Cris Judd from 2001 to 2003. She has twins with her third husband, Marc Anthony, to whom she was married from 2004 to 2014.
She and Ben Affleck, who were previously engaged, married in 2022 and split in 2024.
She was also engaged to Alex Rodriguez; the couple was together from 2017 to 2021.
Lopez poked fun at her weddings in her 2024 music video “Can’t Get Enough.”
During a 2025 interview on the “Howard Stern Show,” she said she felt that she has never been truly loved, but she has loved.

“It’s not that I’m not lovable. It’s that they’re not capable,” she said. “They don’t have it in them. And they gave me what they had, they gave me all of it every time. All the rings, all the things I could ever want. The houses, the rings, the marriage, all of it. But they didn’t love me and I didn’t love myself.”
She said her last divorce was the “best thing that happened to (her).”

title: Robert Pattinson Announced as the New James Bond
summary: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced.
story: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond.

Pattinson will take on the role of film’s most famous British secret agent in the 26th installment of the long-running Bond franchise. The upcoming movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, the mastermind behind the “Dune” trilogy.

Pattinson starred in “The Drama,” “The Odyssey,” “Primetime” and “Dune: Part Three” this year alone. He follows in the footsteps of Daniel Craig, Pierce Brosnan, Timothy Dalton, Roger Moore, Sean Connery and George Lazenby, who all played Bond on the big screen.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement. “... To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”
The announcement comes five years after Craig played the suave spy, whose code name is 007, in the last Bond film, 2021’s “No Time to Die.”
Casting rumors about the new Bond have been making headlines for months.

In October, Deadline reported that several A-list British actors were performing screen tests for the coveted role. Insiders told the publication that top contenders at that time were “One Night Only” star Callum Turner, “Slow Horses” and “White Lotus” actor Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor of “The Crown” and “Challengers.”
Weeks later, Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult were suddenly in the running, according to Variety.
Pop star Harry Styles also engaged in “discussions” about the part, Variety reported.
The Bond character was created in 1952 by British author Ian Fleming, who wrote about the secret agent across 12 novels and two short story collections.
Brosnan, who played Bond from 1995 until 2002, told Vanity Fair he would be pleased to see Turner, his co-star in 2017’s “The Only Living Boy in New York,” take on the role.

“All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire. Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men,” Brosnan said.
“Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage,” Brosnan added.

title: The Most Important Line in ‘The Good Daughter,’ According to Karin Slaughter, Is ‘Not a Message Women Get Often’
summary: Warning: This story contains spoilers for “The Good Daughter.”
story: Warning: This story contains spoilers for “The Good Daughter.”

From the moment two masked men with guns step into the home of teenage sisters Samantha and Charlotte Quinn, it’s clear that crime drama “The Good Daughter” is a story about survival — what happens after violence changes the trajectory of your life, and the pain of piecing together your past.
It’s just one of several traumatic plot points in the six-episode series, based on the book of the same name by bestselling author Karin Slaughter, out Nov. 12 on Peacock.
While sexual violence is a theme in much of Slaughter’s work, extra care was given to how this story was brought to the small screen, Slaughter tells TODAY.com.

“One of the things I’m most proud of in this show is I set these rules that we were only going to tell the story from the perspective of Sam or Charlie,” she says. “If it’s young Charlie, (director Steph Green) would lower the camera angle, and the focus is always on the girls and not on the bad men doing bad things.”

“I’m very mindful that when you see a woman’s body, you think about how you feel, and when you see a man’s body, you think about how the man feels. So I wanted to really make sure that we weren’t being exploitative and we were showing this perspective.”

“The Good Daughter” revolves around the sisters Charlotte “Charlie” and Samantha “Sam,” played by Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne respectively, who are estranged as adults but reunite after one of them becomes unintentionally linked to a murder case. Together, the siblings must contend with the past in order to reconcile and embrace their futures.
Both Byrne and Fahy tell TODAY.com that they were drawn to the project because of the show’s focus on the strength of the characters, rather than on the abuse and suffering that they had endured.

“The show is about hope, and it’s about perseverance, and it’s about confronting the things that scare you, relieving yourself of unnecessary shame, and claiming the life that you really want to have for yourself and the people that you love,” Fahy says.

Byrne adds: “We wanted to celebrate the resilience of all situations like that and all people who survived these horrific events. ... A huge part of the conversation around when I signed on (was) how will this be dealt with? How will this be depicted?”

Both actors were tasked with embodying survivorship in different ways. For Byrne, Sam’s disability from a bullet wound to the head meant two months working on her gait with a physical therapist who rehabilitates similar patients in real life.
Fahy’s character Charlie, meanwhile, has kept a secret about the attack from everyone except her father, Rusty. Asked how she was able to bring that to life, Fahy points to the “responsibly run set.”

“There was a mental health specialist on set every day that was available to all of the actors and all of the crew if anybody needed support,” Fahy says, adding that Green “took very good care of everybody, so that created a super safe space.”
Slaughter hopes the show helps viewers, particularly those who have gone through trauma of their own, feel supported and safe.

“The most important line in the entire series and in the book is when Rusty says, ‘Whatever you did to survive is exactly what you should do,’” Slaughter explains. “That’s not a message women get often. We aren’t usually told, ‘You did the right thing.’ We’re told, ‘Why didn’t you do this? Why didn’t you do that?’”

On its face, “The Good Daughter” may seem like a quintessential thriller about women solving a crime in a small-town. But, according to Slaughter, it relies just as heavily on other warmer storytelling elements, like comedy and family dynamics.

“It’s so important to me to balance the light and dark,” the author says. “There are laugh-out-loud funny moments ... and that was so important for me to carry from the book into the show because, particularly being from the South ... there is that sensibility of even the worst situation you can find humor in.”
Slaughter adds that connection between the two sisters “propels you through the show as much as the whodunit.”
“At its heart, it’s about a family and this universal sense of dislocation and separation that we all feel as we grow up,” she says.
In fact, the least surprising but perhaps most satisfying aspect of the ending is that Sam and Charlie finally accept how much they need each other.

“The thing about writing about complicated, interesting women and not sentimentalizing them is that you have to know, as a viewer, that you trust the writer (is) going to leave you in a good place, and all my books end on a place of hope, and definitely the show ends on that hope too,” Slaughter says.

title: Has Madeline Miller Seen ‘The Odyssey’ Yet? She Told Jenna
summary: Madeline Miller, author of The Song of Achilles and Circe, shares whether she’s seen Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and why she hasn’t yet
story: Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” was practically required viewing for anyone working in the world of Greek mythology. Well, almost anyone.
On the Nov. 12 episode of “Open Book With Jenna,” author Madeline Miller, who is known for her Greek myth retellings, shared that she hasn’t seen the movie (yet).
“I get terrible migraines from large screens,” Miller told Jenna Bush Hager, adding that she’ll be waiting to watch it from the comfort of her home.
“You and I will be the only (ones) to watch it from our home television,” Jenna remarked.
“The Odyssey” has grossed $1.7 billion worldwide. When the movie was released over the summer, fans clamored for tickets for IMAX and 70mm IMAX screenings.
The author said that she’s seen “The Odyssey” through the eyes of friends and family, who report back to her with “all the details.”

“It was actually a total joy to have people reaching out to me and telling me what they thought about it,” Miller said. “I kind of feel like I’ve seen it, but I’ve seen it through the eyes of all the people I love ... it’s the best, honestly.”

Miller’s first book, “The Song of Achilles,” was a retelling of “The Iliad.” Her second, “Circe,” turned a side character of “The Odyssey” into a lead. Circe, played by Samantha Morton, has a pivotal scene in Nolan’s film.
“Circe goes back to my 8th Grade self reading ‘The Odyssey’ for the first time, and being so disappointed in how little page time Circe gets,” Miller said.

She remembers “wanting more” out of the  enchantress’ backstory. “Why is she turning men into pigs? Who is this woman? How did she get that kind of power? What does it mean to be a witch? All of those things had been sitting with me and getting louder and louder in the background,” she said.
After “Song of Achilles” was finished, Miller said it was “so clear” that she had to focus on Circe.
“It was amazing to get to spend seven years living inside Circe’s head,” Miller said.

Her most recent offering is “Mestra,” a novella pulled from Ovid’s “Metamorphoses.” In it, Poseidon grants a young woman incredible powers of shape-shifting, and she uses them, at first, to please her demanding father, and later to free herself from him.
Miller has been struggling with the effects of long COVID and felt she finally had the concentration and energy to work on fiction.
“It feels like this story just exploded out of me. It was such a tremendous joy, even though the story is in many ways unsettling,” she said.

title: Read With Jenna Jr. Is Coming to the Libby App! How to Read the Books — for Free
summary: You’ll soon be able to read Read with Jenna Jr. picks on the Libby app. Here’s how to find them.
story: You’ll soon be able to read Read with Jenna Jr. book picks in the Libby app, making bedtime reading even easier.
In a new partnership, Read with Jenna and The Libby App are joining together to give readers a way to get the latest book club picks at their fingertips.
This year’s Read With Jenna Jr. list had 21 books ranging from young readers through YA.
The Libby App is a free mobile app that lets readers borrow eBooks and audiobooks from their local library.
Upon login, readers will now find Read With Jenna’s curated book list, front and center in the app — an opportunity to read Jenna’s selections for free!
How to find Read With Jenna Jr. books on Libby
It’s easy — all you’ll need is your library card.
Get a library card by applying online or stop by your local branch.
Get on the Libby app from the app store.
Find Read With Jenna books and customized reading guides right on your home screen.
Since 2019, Jenna Bush Hager has chosen a new book for Read With Jenna each month. She started her kid-friendly list in 2023.

Raised by a librarian mom, Jenna loves libraries, which is what makes the partnership so special. “Libraries have always been close to my heart. They’re more than buildings filled with books, they’re community spaces, and gateways to discovery,” she says.

title: See the Star-Studded Lineup to Appear in ‘NBC100: Live Celebration’
summary: An all-star group of television legends from Jerry Seinfeld to Mariska Hargitay is set to celebrate NBC’s 100th anniversary in style.
story: An all-star group of television legends from Jerry Seinfeld to Mariska Hargitay is set to celebrate NBC’s 100th anniversary in style.

NBC announced the first wave of the star-studded lineup that will be part of “NBC100: The Live Celebration,” a broadcast special airing on Dec. 10 at 8 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock in honor of the network’s anniversary.

Among those appearing are Seinfeld, Hargitay, David Letterman, Conan O’Brien, Jimmy Fallon, Larry David, Simone Biles, Tina Fey, Ted Danson, Michael Phelps and more.

The three-hour live event from the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles will celebrate the television characters, comedy legends and athletes who have made NBC part of the fabric of American culture for a century. It will feature musical performances, surprise reunions and flashbacks to iconic NBC moments, plus appearances by stars of classic NBC shows like “ER,” “The Office,” “Parks and Recreation,” “Law & Order,” “30 Rock” and “Saturday Night Live.”

title: Michael J. Fox, Tracy Pollan and All 3 Daughters Stun in Rare Red Carpet Appearance Together
summary: Michael J. Fox posed with wife and fellow actor Tracy Pollan, along with all three of their daughters, Esmé Annabelle Fox, 25, and twins Schuyler Fox and Aquinnah Kathleen Fox, 31, in a rare appearance together at his annual gala.
story: It’s a family affair!
Actor Michael J. Fox hit the red carpet on Nov. 14 with his family for his foundation’s annual gala, “A Funny Thing Happened On The Way To Cure Parkinson’s” event in New York City.

The 65-year-old posed with wife and fellow actor Tracy Pollan, along with all three of their daughters, Esmé Annabelle Fox, 25, and twins Schuyler Fox and Aquinnah Kathleen Fox, 31, in a rare appearance all together. The couple’s son, Sam Michael Fox, was not in attendance.

Michael J. Fox, who founded the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research in 2000, sported a T-shirt under a more formal jacket. Meanwhile, Pollan and the couple’s daughters rocked stunning gowns for the event.

The night was a particularly eventful one, as it not only featured star-studded attendees from Stephen Colbert and David Letterman to TODAY’s Willie Geist, but also several comedy and musical performances.
Among those to take the stage were John Mayer, Brad Paisley and Michael J. Fox himself, who rocked out on the electric guitar.
Comedians, including Josh Johnson and Tom Papa, also performed sets throughout the night.

Fox has been a vocal proponent of Parkinson’s research. In September, he was awarded the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award at the Emmys for his philanthropy. In his acceptance speech, Fox offered some hopeful remarks.
